# SegaSonic The Hedgehog (MAME set 'sonic', Japan rev. C) - V60 program symbols
#
# Addresses and names only: no game data lives in this file.
# Format:  ADDRESS  KIND  NAME  [LAYOUT]   [# comment]
#   KIND: func = function entry, code = code label, data = data label
# Addresses use the copy of each ROM chip the code refers to:
#   000000-01FFFF (ic17), 080000-09FFFF (ic8), 100000-17FFFF (ic18 + ic9)
# Mirrors are accepted and folded (e.g. FFFFF0 -> 09FFF0).
#
# LAYOUT, for data tables that hold code addresses the analysis cannot see the code load:
#   record=N        the table is an array of N-byte records
#   count=N         ... of N records, or
#   count=prefix    ... of as many records as the 16-bit word before them says, or
#   end=XXXX        ... closed by this 16-bit word where the next record would start
#   code=A,B        every record holds a 32-bit code address at these offsets (0 = no code);
#                   A:BASE is a 16-bit offset from BASE instead
#   lists=N         the table is N 16-bit offsets, from its own address, to such arrays
#   pointers=N      the table is N 32-bit addresses of such arrays
# Sizes, offsets and counts are decimal; end and BASE are hexadecimal, like the data and addresses.
#
# FILE lines lay the functions out in the files of src/ (tools/decompile.py source_files):
#   ADDRESS  file  PATH   # what the stretch holds
# the functions from ADDRESS up to the next file line go to src/PATH.c (PATH has a folder: player/states).
# A file may take several stretches; its functions go in the order of their addresses, and the comment
# of its first line is its description (the Description of the file's header).

# ======== source files: the files of src/ and the stretches of the program each takes (decompile.source_files) ========
# The files by subject: system/, video/, engine/, stage/, player/, objects/ (one a stage), scenes/. A
# stretch is a run of functions the original's linker laid out together; where a module of the
# original ends (its tables after the code, or a 00 byte that aligns the next routine: the *_padding
# data lines), a stretch ends. A routine the linker left among another subject's has its own stretch.
000000  file  system/main              # the machine's main program: power-on and boot, the frame loop, the attract mode and the system modes, the frame wait and the controls, the interrupt handlers, the reset vector
000652  file  stage/game_modes         # the game modes (run_game_mode) and what a stage frame runs: starting a stage, layer blending, the stage clear check, the player summary, stage slots and events, restart points, the player objects, the GAME OVER banner and the demo prompt
0018B6  file  engine/contacts          # contacts between objects and players: the zones, the hitter, touchable, rider, platform and wall lists, and the checks that pair them

# The frame loop: every frame of the game starts when wait_for_frame returns. It polls 7000[R25], which
# the VBLANK end interrupt decrements, and then falls into read_controls.
098EC6  func  wait_for_frames      # 7000[R25] = 7001[R25] (frames_per_wait: 0, so one frame; only the unused init_sprites_swapping_every_frame sets 1), then wait_for_frame
098ECE  func  wait_for_frame  # Waits for the next frame: sets sprite_list_ready, polls until irq_vblank_end has counted frames_to_wait below 0, reloads it from frames_per_wait,...
098ED6  code  frame_wait_loop
098EDE  code  frame_wait_done
098EFB  func  read_controls        # ports, then the three trackballs into 7062[R25]..706D[R25]

# Stage objects. 706E[R25] holds the stage number and 6435[R25] how far the stage has scrolled; both
# spawners walk the current stage's list and start every object whose position has been reached.
# A new object runs the handler stored at 1C of its slot ("jsr [1C[R20]]" in the object loop).
100000  data  object_types             record=8 count=45 code=4   # +0 a word read into 8[R25], +4 handler
struct object_type_record 8 rom            # an object_types record (object_types + object_type x 8: spawn_objects_by_type 08DC9A-08DCA4 "movea.b 100000, R8; mul.w #8, R7; add.w R7, R8"): it reads "mov.w [R8+], R1" (08DCA7; its low half into spawn_count, "mov.h R1, 8[R25]") and, after spawn_object_with_pieces, "mov.w [R8], 1C[R20]" (08DCD1); census ROM 100000-100167 (45 types)
field object_type_record 00 part_count u32  # spawn_count for spawn_object_with_pieces (the object and its pool 2 pieces): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, A
field object_type_record 04 handler u32     # the new object's handler (1C): 00EC9E-01586E (vine_init, fence_post_init, centipede_init...)
100168  data  stage_spawns_by_type     # 19 pointers, one per stage, to lists of 14-byte records: scroll position,
                                       # projected_x (2A), projected_y (2C), z, object type (index into object_types), 92, 94; FFFF ends
struct type_spawn_record E rom             # a stage_spawns_by_type record (type_spawn_cursor): spawn_objects_by_type 08DC75 "movz.hw [R10+], R1" (cmp.h #FFFF, then cmp.w with scroll_position: unsigned), 08DC86 "movz.hw [R10+], R4", 08DC89 / 08DC8C "movs.hw [R10+]" into R5 / R6, 08DC97 "movz.hw [R10+], R7", 08DCD6 / 08DCDC "mov.h [R10+]" into 92 / 94; 14 bytes a record ("add.w #E, [R25]" 08DC91); census ROM 1001B4-10162D (369 records)
field type_spawn_record 00 position u16     # the scroll_position it spawns at (once passed); FFFF ends the list
field type_spawn_record 02 projected_x u16  # into projected_x (2A): 13AE, 144E...
field type_spawn_record 04 projected_y s16  # sign-extended, << 16 into projected_y (2C): FCCE, FD1E...
field type_spawn_record 06 z s16            # sign-extended, << 16 into z (40): 0-530
field type_spawn_record 08 object_type u16  # its object_types record (x 8): 0-2C
field type_spawn_record 0A spawn_arg_1 u16  # into spawn_arg_1 (92)
field type_spawn_record 0C spawn_arg_2 u16  # into spawn_arg_2 (94)
081224  data  stage_spawns_by_handler  lists=19 record=12 end=FFFF code=8   # position, 4E, 52, 04, handler
struct handler_spawn_record C rom          # a stage_spawns_by_handler record (handler_spawn_cursor): spawn_objects_by_handler "cmp.h [R10], 6435[R25]" + bl (080023: unsigned), "sub.h [R10], R0" (080031), then from + 2 "mov.h [R10+]" into 4E, 52 and 04 (08004D, 080057, 080061) and "mov.w [R10+], 1C[R11]" (080066); 12 bytes a record ("add.w #C, 70DA[R25]" 08006B); census ROM 08124A-082063 (298 records, FFFF ends each list)
field handler_spawn_record 00 position u16  # the scroll_position it spawns at; skipped once 100 or more behind
field handler_spawn_record 02 x u16         # into x_int (4E), x_fraction 0: 0, 1248...
field handler_spawn_record 04 y u16         # into y_int (52), y_fraction 0
field handler_spawn_record 06 handler_arg u16  # into sprite_frame (04), a parameter the handler reads (stage_03_floor_block_start's block kind, sign_start's kind): 0-17
field handler_spawn_record 08 handler u32   # into handler (1C): 009B4D-094C3F
01F206  data  stage_template_spawns    # func_01E37E: 19 offsets to lists of 12-byte records: position, offset
                                       # into stage_object_templates, count, x, y, dx, dy; FFFF ends
01F4D2  data  stage_object_templates   record=26 count=6 code=18   # 2, 4, 6, 10, 82, 44-47, 48, handler, 64-66
093269  data  stage_object_records     record=22 count=23 code=6   # 2, 4, 6, handler, 48 (data), 10, 12, 64, 65, 96
093EC9  data  stage_record_spawns      # func_09383A: 19 offsets to lists of 14- or 24-byte records by type;
                                       # the 24-byte ones index stage_object_records_2 at +22; FFFF ends
093F59  data  stage_object_records_2   record=24 count=4 code=6   # 2, 4, 6, handler, 48, 48 alternative, 10, 12, 96

# A 16-bit count and that many handlers: func_001CFD and func_001CF1 start one object per player slot
# (400[R25] + 200 each); the handlers set 9A to the player number

                                                                     # +12 the child's 10, 12, 7C, 7D, handler, 48

struct machine_fireball_spawns 2 rom     # spawns_with_next_handler (08530D): the count of the fireballs machine_fire_update spawns once the machine is wrecked, their records (machine_fireball_spawn) after it: "movea.b 8530D[PC], R12" (083670)
field machine_fireball_spawns 00 count u16  # 4: "cmp.h 6900[R25], [R12]" (083675, against free_object_stack), "mov.h [R12+], 70EA[R25]" (08367D, the loop's count)
struct machine_fireball_spawn E rom      # one fireball of spawns_with_next_handler (after its count): machine_fire_update copies it with [R12+] (083697-0836C1); census ROM 08530F-085346
field machine_fireball_spawn 00 x s16     # "mov.h [R12+], 4E[R11]" (083697): x_int F6FA, F6DA
field machine_fireball_spawn 02 y s16     # "mov.h [R12+], 52[R11]" (0836A1): y_int 0A80
field machine_fireball_spawn 04 target_x s16  # "mov.h [R12+], 96[R11]" (0836AB): fireball_start.target_x F74C, F700
field machine_fireball_spawn 06 target_y s16  # "mov.h [R12+], 9A[R11]" (0836B1): fireball_start.target_y 0AC0, 0AF7, 0B30, 0AEE
field machine_fireball_spawn 08 z s16     # "mov.h [R12+], 42[R11]" (0836B7): z_int 04A0, 04B0, 0490, 0470
field machine_fireball_spawn 0A next_handler u32  # "mov.w [R12+], 9C[R11]" (0836C1): 083BAB, 083B35
                                                                        # 9C, the handler 083B14 moves into 1C

# ======== Names for the decompiled C (tools/decompile.py) ========
# Besides functions and labels, symbols.txt names what the decompiled C reads and writes:
#   register RN NAME              a register the whole program shares (a global variable in C)
#   ADDRESS var NAME TYPE         a variable in work RAM          TYPE: u8 s8 u16 s16 u32 s32
#   ADDRESS io NAME TYPE          a register of the board
#   ADDRESS table NAME TYPE       data in the program ROM the code reads by index (TYPE per element)
#   ADDRESS table NAME STRUCT     a table of the program ROM's records, read by index: name[i].field
#   elements NAME TYPE [STRUCT]   values of the program ROM a pointer walks: NAME(p)[i] (STRUCT: what each points at)
#   struct NAME SIZE              a structure in work RAM (SIZE in hexadecimal)
#   struct NAME SIZE rom          a record of the program ROM, read through a pointer: NAME(p)->field, NAME(p)[i].field
#   field STRUCT OFFSET NAME TYPE one of its fields (OFFSET in hexadecimal); TYPE[N] an array of N in it,
#                                 TYPE[] one after a record's end: NAME(p)->field[i]
#   scoped STRUCT FAMILY OFFSET NAME TYPE  a field as the code of one family of functions (whose names
#                                 start with FAMILY) uses it in the structure it runs on (an object type's own variables)
#   scoped global FAMILY ADDRESS NAME TYPE  work RAM as one family of functions uses it (scratch variables)
#   param FUNCTION RN NAME        what a function takes or hands back in register RN; its callers name the
#                                 variables they pass in RN, or get back from it, the same way
#   result FUNCTION RN NAME       what a function nothing calls hands back in register RN (its callers say
#                                 it for the others); every register such a function reads before writing
#                                 is one of its parameters
#   constant FUNCTION VALUE NAME  a number the function uses, by name (VALUE in hexadecimal; a #define in ram.h)
#   local FUNCTION WHERE RN NAME  the local variable that holds what the instructions at WHERE (addresses,
#                                 or "entry": where the function starts) write in register RN
# A second var or field at the same place with a narrower type names the first bytes of the wider one
# (x_fraction: the low half of the 16.16 x).
# A struct name after the TYPE of a var or field says its value points at one: a u32 holds the address,
# a u16 the low half of it (the game links its structures in the work RAM page by 16-bit addresses).
# "rom" after a u32 says it points into the program ROM.
# Whatever has no name yet appears as unk_ADDRESS, rom_ADDRESS, VIDEO_ADDRESS... or unk_OFFSET in C.

# -- the registers the whole program keeps things in --
register R18  current_player        # the player block being run (0x208400 + 0x200 per player); some code keeps other things in it: the player's object (shadow_update, draw_attack_effect), a row count (build_ranking_display)
register R20  current_object        # the object being run: the object loop sets it before its handler
register R21  free_objects          # mostly the stack of free objects (0x20E900); also a counter at times
register R22  first_object          # the object list's first ...
register R23  object_cursor         # ... the object loop's position in it ...
register R24  last_object           # ... and its last
register R26  fill_value            # what the string moves (MOVCFU) fill with
register R32  stack_pointer         # SP, in the functions whose stack stays in memory (decompiler/stack.py: code the game never calls uses its stack frame as an array); 20FF00 after boot

# -- objects: a doubly linked list of 0xA0-byte blocks in work RAM, linked by 16-bit addresses --
207FE0  var  object_count   u16     # one more when an object joins the list, one less when it leaves
207FE2  var  first_object_address  u32 object
207FE6  var  last_object_address   u32 object
20E900  var  free_object_stack     s16 object     # [0] how many are free, then their 16-bit addresses  (TYPE: 26 of its 30 uses compare it signed, "(int16_t)free_object_stack < n" before spawning)
20EA10  var  free_object_stack_2   s16 object     # the same for a second pool  (TYPE: 9 signed compares of [0], 3 == 0 tests, the rest pushes/pops)
struct object A0
field object 1C handler    u32      # the code the object loop runs for it
field object 20 previous   u16 object      # 16-bit address of the object before it in the list
field object 22 next       u16 object      # ... and after it
field object 34 speed_x    s32      # 16.16 fixed point, added to x every frame
field object 34 speed_x_fraction u16  # the low half of speed_x (16.16)
field object 36 speed_x_int s16         # the whole part of speed_x: pixels a frame
field object 38 speed_y    s32
field object 38 speed_y_fraction u16
field object 3A speed_y_int s16         # the whole part of speed_y
field object 3C speed_z    s32      # vertical: gravity adds 0x6000 a frame; a jump sets it to -8.0
field object 3C speed_z_fraction u16
field object 3E speed_z_int s16         # the whole part of speed_z
field object 40 z          s32      # height
field object 40 z_fraction u16
field object 42 z_int s16               # the whole part of z
field object 4C x          s32
field object 4C x_fraction u16         # the low half of x: the code clears it to put an object on a whole pixel
field object 4E x_int s16               # the whole part of x
field object 50 y          s32
field object 50 y_fraction u16
field object 52 y_int s16               # the whole part of y
field object 9A player     u8       # the player the object belongs to (player handlers set it)

# -- players: 0x200-byte blocks from 0x208400, one per player --
struct player 200

# -- the frame loop --
20F000  var  frames_to_wait   s8    # wait_for_frame polls it; the VBLANK end interrupt counts it down
20F001  var  frames_per_wait  u8    # wait_for_frames copies it into frames_to_wait; 0003DD and init_sprites set it to 0
20F061  var  game_mode        u8    # the main dispatcher (func_000652) switches on it; 8 is stage select
20F06E  var  stage            u16   # the stage being played (the protection writes it, see below)
20E5C4  var  cleared_stages   u16   # writing it makes the protection device (FD1149) pick the next stage

# -- the I/O chip (315-5296) --
C00000  io  io_port_a     u8        # player 1 button (bit 0), player 3 button (bit 2)
C00002  io  io_port_b     u8        # player 2 button (bit 0)
C00004  io  io_port_c     u8
C00006  io  io_port_d     u8        # outputs: coin counters; EEPROM data in (bit 7), chip select (5), clock (6)
C00008  io  io_port_e     u8        # service, test, coins 1-2, starts 1-2, coin 3, start 3
C0000A  io  io_port_f     u8        # DIP switches (bits 0-3), PCB buttons (4-5), EEPROM data out (bit 7)
C0000C  io  io_port_g     u8
C0000E  io  io_port_h     u8        # the external tile bank
C0001C  io  io_cnt        u8        # bit 1 turns the display on, bit 2 lets the sound CPU run
C0001E  io  io_direction  u8        # the ports used as outputs

# -- the interrupt controller --
D00007  io  irq_acknowledge  u8
D00008  io  timer_0_reload   u16
D0000A  io  timer_1_reload   u16

# -- functions --
0991C1  func  run_objects           # from the last object through the list: R20 = object, jsr [1C[R20]]
099246  func  allocate_object       # R0 = how many were free (0: none); R11 = the object
099353  func  allocate_object_2     # the same from the second pool
09C724  func  eeprom_read_all       # 0x40 words into 7600[R25]
09C79C  func  eeprom_read_word  # Reads one EEPROM word: eeprom_send_command(command), then 0x12 clocks reading port_f bit 7, then eeprom_deselect; hands back the 16-bit word in...
09C7CB  func  eeprom_write_word     # then waits for the chip to say it is ready (data out high)
09C82B  func  eeprom_send_command  # Starts an EEPROM command on port_d: lines low, a clock, chip select up, then the start bit and command's 8 bits, high bit first, each on the data...
09C87B  func  eeprom_select         # R13 = port D, R12 = port F; interrupts off
09C8E0  func  eeprom_deselect  # Clears the EEPROM's chip select, clock and data lines (bits 5-7 of lines) on port_d and hands back lines
09C8E4  func  eeprom_set_lines      # writes R2 to port D

# ======== system (from build/naming/system.txt) ========
# System and hardware: proposals from the system helper (symbols.txt syntax, one per line, "# evidence")
#
# How it works (summary; details in the comments):
# - boot: copies 8 byte pairs from 00007E to E00000 (unmapped on this board, MAME and s32ref ignore them) and
#   00 01 02 03 04 00 00 00 FF FF FF FF from 00008E to D00000-D0000B (vectors 0-4, D00005 = 0, mask 0, acknowledge
#   all, both timers 0xFFF). Then delay_after_reset, init_system, and the loop: wait_for_frame + run_frame, or,
#   while test_mode is set, start_test_mode + wait_for_frame + run_test_mode; leaving test mode sets
#   system_mode_step/system_mode to 0/3 (the title) and runs init_system again.
# - run_frame (once per frame): frame_counter++, outside system modes 0 and 6 checks coin starts (credits >=
#   credits_per_start and the start button, or the attack button when setting_no_start_buttons is set: then
#   system_mode 6, game_mode 0, game_in_progress FF), runs system_mode_handlers[system_mode], run_objects,
#   build_sprite_list, draw_queued_strings.
# - system_mode (20F007): 0 attract_warning (power-on, 10 s), 1 system_mode_idle (never selected), 2 attract_ranking,
#   3 attract_title, 4 attract_demo_1, 5 attract_demo_2, 6 run_game_mode (the game), 7 wait_attract_timer.
#   advance_attract_screen walks attract_sequence (2 3 4 2 3 5 3 5 ...); s32ref attract: warning 0-602, ranking
#   602-1361, title 1361-2289, demo 1 2289-2866 (0x240 frames), ranking, title, demo 2 4553-5130, ...
# - game_mode (20F061), case labels below: 0/33 start game -> 1B character select -> 1 intro -> 2 start_stage ->
#   3 play; stage events switch to the scripted modes (stages.txt); the stage end goes 23 (stage clear) -> 29
#   (results) -> 4 (fade, next stage) or, on stages B-F, 30; all players out -> 7 game over (back to attract
#   after 0x78 frames). Nothing sets game_mode 9, 0x0B, 0x0E (the global "CONTINUE ?") or 0x0F: continues are
#   per player (player state 0x23, players.txt). current_game_mode (20E5A9) is the copy the rest of the program
#   tests.
# - Interrupts (vector 0x40 + n): VBLANK start: the mixer shadow (20F1C0, mixer_text_blend on) -> 610030, run_vblank_copies, vblank_start_hook
#   (apply_video_registers), send_sound_command, and outside test mode count_frames_and_check_test_switch and,
#   unless free_play, update_coins; display_off_frames; acknowledge bit 0. VBLANK end: vblank_hook (20F100,
#   swap_sprite_buffers) unless debug_pause, frames_to_wait--, acknowledge bit 1. Sound: acknowledge bit 2 only.
#   Timers 0/1: count timer_0_ticks/timer_1_ticks (never read), reload 0x32/0x23, acknowledge bits 3/4.
# - Sound: play_sound/queue_sound put ids in a 32-entry ring (sound_queue); every VBLANK send_sound_command takes
#   one id and writes the two bytes of sound_commands[id] to the shared RAM mailbox: 700701 = group, 700700 =
#   number. Groups: 80 control (id 96 = 80 01, queued by init_sound: probably reset; 94 = 80 03 and 95 = 80 00,
#   queued before every sound test sound, at test mode entry, game over...), 81 music (ids 0-4, 7B-7E, 81, 82,
#   8D-93), 82 effects (ids 5-2E, 7F = the coin sound, 83-89, 8B, 8C), 83 a third set (ids 2F-7A, 80, 8A,
#   probably voices/PCM). The Z80 program spins at 012D while sound_cpu_hold (Z80 FFFF) is not 0. The program
#   never writes D0000C-D0000F (s32ref: 0 sound requests): the Z80 polls the mailbox.
# - Battery-backed shared RAM (701F00-701FFF; the CRCs and backup copies only make sense if it survives power
#   off): the bookkeeping block 701F02-701F41 (CRC at 701F00, copy at 701F42-701F81), the ranking 701F82-701FF9
#   (CRC at 701FFA), the DIP 1 state (701FFE) and sound_cpu_hold (701FFF). All CRCs are compute_crc16
#   (polynomial 1021, seeded DEBDEB); the program's own ROM checks reproduce the four rom_checksums exactly
#   (verified in Python on build/rom/program.bin).
# - EEPROM (93C46, 0x40 words) shadow at 20F600-20F67F: header 'A23S', ROM stamp, CRC of 760A-763F, write count,
#   the settings 760E-7627, and a full backup copy at 20F640. load_settings: magic wrong -> defaults (magic 'SEGA':
#   defaults and write count 100); ROM stamp changed -> settings reset (760E-763F from the defaults); bad CRC ->
#   the backup if its CRC is good, else settings reset; then saved. Defaults (09C580): advertise sound off,
#   1 coin 1 credit, common chutes, 2P cabinet, 1 credit to start, difficulty 2/4, vitality 2/4.
# - Coins: update_coins (VBLANK) counts coins on release (inputs_released bits 2, 3, 6 = coin 1, 2, 3; service
#   bit 0 or the PCB service button bit 12 gives a service credit), with chute multipliers, bonus adder and
#   coins per credit, credits max 9, three credit blocks of 4 bytes at 20F412/416/41A (common chutes use the
#   first), pulses the two coin counters (port D bits 0/1, 6 frames on and 6 off per coin), plays sound 7F,
#   saves credits into the bookkeeping. COIN/CREDIT SETTING 26 (bonus adder 1) is free play.
# - DIP switch 1 (port F bit 0, low = on) is the moving seat cabinet: check_moving_seat_dip keeps its state in
#   moving_seat_dip (701FFE) and the test menu then shows OUTPUT TEST (port D bits 2/3 = 1P/2P seat) and the
#   MOVING SEAT option.
# - Port D (outputs): bits 0-1 coin counters, 2-3 the seats (OUTPUT TEST), 4 set at init, 5-7 EEPROM; bit 3 is
#   also cleared by init_sound (unreached code at 09A593 sets it when sound is allowed).

# ======== boot, frame loop, system modes ========
0000DF  func  run_frame                 # boot's loop calls it every frame unless test_mode: frame_counter++, start checks (credits >= credits_per_start, cabinet_config switch) outside system modes 0/6, system_mode_handlers[system_mode], run_objects, build_sprite_list, then jmp draw_queued_strings
0003DD  func  init_system               # boot calls it at power-on and after test mode: interrupts off, clear_work_ram, init_io_ports, init_sound, load_settings, load_bookkeeping, apply_settings, init_mixer, load_default_palettes, init_sprites, load_text_font, init_video_registers, three read_controls, D00007 = 0 (acknowledge all), D00005 = 0, check_moving_seat_dip, init_game_settings, interrupts on
0004DB  func  clear_work_ram            # zeroes 208000-20FDFF (0xFC x 0x80 bytes), saving and restoring the halfword at 20F006 (system_mode_step/system_mode)
00049E  func  init_io_ports             # port D = 10, G = 0, H = 0, CNT = 80, direction = C8 (D, G, H outputs), twice; cabinet_events = 1F

08F0EA  func  load_ranking              # init_game_settings: ranking = saved_ranking (701F82, 0x78 bytes) when compute_crc16 of it matches ranking_checksum, else reset_ranking

08EC87  func  enter_ranking_initials    # player state 0x2E (game over, from 0050D4): the trackball changes the letter (codes 0-2B), the button (bit number in 80[R20]) goes to the next (93, up to 3), 84 counts down; then the record (value 34, 36-3B) is sorted into ranking (lowest first), initials 'sex'/'xxx'/'x x'/'xx ' become 'tak' (08EEA1), ranking -> saved_ranking + ranking_checksum

701F16  io    bookkeeping_power_on_time_high  u16

# ======== objects (from build/naming/objects.txt) ========
# Proposals: the object system and drawing (objects, sprites, projection, collision, movement)
# Format as in symbols.txt; every line carries its evidence. Addresses are the ones the C and the listing use.
# "Reference run" = build/bin/s32ref.exe with tests/controls/stage_00.txt (frame 3700 dumped and --watch).

# ======== struct object (0xA0 bytes) ========
# 00-1B is a sprite descriptor that build_sprite_list (09A27B) turns into one 16-byte System 32 sprite
# entry. Pool 2 blocks (0x30 bytes, see allocate_object_2) only have 00-2F.
# 7E-9F (except 9A) are each object type's own variables: 80-8C are timers, counters, step indexes
# (08E49E, 08E7FD, 01E86E), 92/94 come from the stage list (08DC63), 9C is the creator's return address
# for spawn_objects (08DD56) and a "next handler" for the objects 083B14 restarts. Not named here.
field object 00 draw_next u16 object          # next object in the same depth bucket: the queue_sprite_* routines (099FC0...) push the object with "mov.h [bucket],[R20]"; build_sprite_list follows it until it points back at the bucket
field object 02 sprite_flags u16       # word 0 of the sprite entry (MAME segas32_v: 13 indirect palette, 11 shadow, 9 8bpp, 8 pen 0 transparent, 7 y flip, 6 x flip, 5/4 add the y/x offset set by entry 1 (screen centre 70/A0), 3-2 y anchor (1 bottom), 1-0 x anchor (0 centre)); 00DFC1/00E058 negate dx/dy with bits 6/7. The game reuses bits 15,14,12 to pick how 09A27B writes it: 000 scaled frame, 001 unscaled frame (0x1004 is the usual value), 01x the 16 bytes 02-11 as they are (clip entries, 0x5000), 100 a jump to the next entry (unused), 101 sized frame (18/1A sizes, 08 = address), 110/111 multi-part sprite (0xC000/0xD00x). init_object_fields sets 4
field object 04 sprite_frame u16 wall_kind_parts@wall_kinds+6       # offset of the frame's 4-word record (width, height + address bits, bank bits, address) in sprite_frame_records (7112[R25] = 0x130000); 00DEB3 & co. load it from the animation. Multi-part sprites keep a 32-bit pointer to a part list in 04-07 (count <= 16, then per part frame, flags, s8 dx, s8 dy, palette: 09A3F2). The walls' spawner keeps its wall kind's byte offset into wall_kinds in it (spawn_walls tests that kind's second_sprite at wall_kind_second_sprites + it), hence its link: a wall_kind_parts record that many bytes from wall_kinds + 6
field object 04 part_list u32            # multi-part sprites (flags 0xC000/0xD00x): the 32-bit address of the part list in 04-07, in place of sprite_frame and sprite_palette
field object 06 sprite_palette u16     # word 7 of the sprite entry (09A2CB "mov.h 6[R20],[R19+]"): palette; the bits above it pick the mixer's priority group (00C2C7 copies the player's bits 13-14 to its extra sprites, 01E4ED moves a shadow to 0x2000); xFFE is the shadow colour (shadows use 9FFE/1FFE)
field object 08 sprite_scale u16       # 0x100 = 1:1: 09A317 multiplies both frame sizes by it (+0x80, >>8); init_object_fields sets 0x100; 01E9C1 shrinks rings by 0x10 a frame. Sized frames (flags 9xxx) use it as the address word instead (0953BF loads it from the frame record +6)
field object 0A sprite_layer u16       # low byte = depth bucket for queue_sprite_in_layer (099FF9); HUD objects set 0-9 just before calling it (01C3D4 6, 01C53A 5, 095B0B 1)
field object 0C screen_y s16           # sprite entry word 4 (09A2C2 "mov.w C[R20]" writes 0C then 0E); update_screen_position: (projected_y + z) >> 16 - view_y + sprite_offset_y. Reference run: player 137 = 495 - 368 + 10
field object 0E screen_x s16           # sprite entry word 5; projected_x - view_x + sprite_offset_x (player 104 = 233 - 129 + 0)
field object 10 hitbox_size_x u16      # box hitboxes span x + hitbox_offset_x .. + this (check_hit 001E6A, check_zones 0018E5, check_walls 0022E7); round hitboxes (flags bit 1 clear) use it as the radius (001F64: radius sum, squared distance)
field object 12 hitbox_size_y u16      # the box along y (001E97, 001900); round hitboxes use its two bytes as s8 centre offsets in x (12) and y (13) (001F78, 001F9D)
field object 14 anchor_x s16           # 00DFC1: projected_x = this + the animation step's dx; handlers copy projected_x here first (080EA8, 088D5D, 08CB40). check_zones stores the touching partner here instead (00193C), which 00CF6A reads
field object 16 anchor_y s16           # 00DFC1: integer part of projected_y = this + the step's dy
field object 18 sprite_height s16      # sized frames (flags 9xxx): ORed into entry word 2, the height on screen (09A386); 0953BF sets it  (TYPE: 4 of its 5 reads are signed: player_update/player_animate, shadow_update and draw_opening_machine_shadow keep a signed y offset here that they scale by the zoom; only build_sprite_list ORs it)
field object 1A sprite_width s16       # sized frames: ORed into entry word 3, the width on screen (09A373)  (TYPE: the same scaled x offsets, and player_hud_update and message_box_show compare it signed; only build_sprite_list ORs it)
field object 24 direction u16          # angle, 0x400 a turn: set_speed_from_direction gives speed_x = sine[24] * speed, speed_y = -cosine[24] * speed (0 = towards -y, 0x100 = towards +x); face_nearest_player sets it (about towards player 1: see there)
field object 26 parent u16 object             # 16-bit address of the object that created it: spawn_objects/spawn_object_with_pieces store R23 (object_cursor); pool 2 pieces get the main object (08DDB2); 082E82, 01E37E too
field object 28 child u16 object              # first object of the chain this object owns, FFFF = none; the chain goes on through each child's 28 (08DDAE, 01E37E: a ring's shadow); delete_object_and_children frees the whole chain
field object 2A projected_x s16        # project_object: ((x + y) >> 8) * 0xB5 >> 16, the isometric screen x before the camera; unproject_object turns 2A/2C back into x/y
field object 2C projected_y s32        # project_object: ((y - x) >> 9) * 0xB5, 16.16: screen y of the ground point (2E = whole pixels); screen_y adds z; sprites queued at their floor sort by it
field object 2C projected_y_fraction u16
field object 2E projected_y_int s16     # the whole part of projected_y (16.16): the screen y of the ground point
field object 30 flags u32              # bits: 1 box hitbox (else round), 2 touched (check_hit sets it on both, the other in touched_by), 3 on a platform (check_platforms, the other in platform), 4 was on a platform last frame (00B5C6), 5 against a wall (check_walls, the other in wall), 6 hit by an attacking player (00E488 sets it on the touched object; the player handlers also set it on themselves), 7 animate backwards (00DEB3), 9 players ignore its touches (00E488; scattered rings for their first 0x1E frames), 10 player out of the game (08DCEC, 001A7F, 002CEC), 11 has been on screen (01F0EF), 27 touched in check_zones (the other in anchor_x). The player handlers use other bits for their own states; timer objects use byte 0 as "started" and the high word as a frame counter (0973B4)
field object 44 animation_speed u8     # frames per animation step: animate reloads animation_timer from it
field object 45 animation_timer s8     # counted down every frame by animate (00DEA2) and the other animate_* routines; the step advances when it runs out (reference run, player: 2C, 2B ... 01, then 46 = 6 and 2C again)
field object 46 animation_frame u8     # index of the current step (animate_step: + 1, wraps to 0 after the last step number; - 1 with flags bit 7)
field object 47 kind u8                # what the object is to collisions: 0-2 the players (002808 copies player into it), 3 ring (01E709, all stage_object_templates), 9 object_steps (082E82), 0xC the most common enemy kind...; check_hit skips pairs where both are 0-2; the player switches on the touched object's kind (00E488, 00CF6A)
field object 48 animation u32          # ROM pointer to the animation: a word (last step number in its low byte), then the steps (animate_step: frames; 00DE60: flags + frame; 00DEFD/00DF72/00DFF5: frame, dx, dy)
field object 54 floor_z s32            # z of the floor under the object (same units as z; larger = lower): find_floor sets it from the floor block (+10) and its slope; 0x800 = no floor (no_floor_block); fall_to_floor lands z on it; check_platforms compares riders with a platform's 56
field object 54 floor_z_fraction u16
field object 56 floor_z_int s16         # the whole part of floor_z
field object 58 previous_floor_z s32   # find_floor saves floor_z here before replacing it (while floor_block >= 0 and the floor < 0x7FF); 01E8C8 and the player restore it when they step back
field object 58 previous_floor_z_fraction u16
field object 5A previous_floor_z_int s16   # the whole part of previous_floor_z
field object 5C floor_block s32        # offset of the floor block under the object in floor_blocks (from +2), -1 = none (find_floor). Reference run: player 0x16 (the second 22-byte block)
field object 60 previous_floor_block s32   # find_floor saves floor_block here; restored together with previous_floor_z (01E8C8, 00C920). Timer objects use byte 61 as their list index (0973B4)
field object 64 sprite_offset_x s8     # added to screen_x (00C50D "+ (int8_t)AS8(unk_64)"); stage_object_templates and the spawners set it (01E37E, 09383A 0x2E)
field object 65 sprite_offset_y s8     # added to screen_y (00C50D); queue_sprite_at_base takes it back off for the depth. Player: 0x0A
field object 66 hitbox_height u16      # how far the hitbox reaches above z: check_hit 00205F needs "42 - 66" of each <= the other's 42; check_walls compares the height difference with it. Player: 0x18, rings: 0x20
field object 68 hit_list_next u16 object      # link in the hitter, touchable and zone lists (0020A5, 0020C2, 001956 push the object; 001DDD, 001E33, 0018B6 walk until a negative value)
field object 6A touched_by u16 object         # check_hit (00208A) stores each object of a touching pair in the other's touched_by; the player reads its kind (00E488), rings read it to find the player that took them (01E4ED)
field object 6E speed s32              # speed along direction: set_speed_from_direction uses its high word (70), 0x100 there = 1 pixel a frame; scattered rings get 0x800000-0xFFFFFF (01E709)
field object 6E speed_fraction u16
field object 70 speed_int s16           # the high word of speed: 0x100 is 1 pixel a frame
field object 72 platform_list_next u16 object # link in the rider, platform and wall lists (0020DB, 0020F4, 0022A6 push; 002108 and 0022BA walk)
field object 74 platform u16 object           # check_platforms (002178): on a rider the platform it stands on, on the platform the rider; find_floor takes floor_block and floor_z (the platform's z) from it while flags bit 3 is set
field object 76 floor_slope u8         # slope type of the floor block (+13), index into floor_slopes: find_floor adds the slope to floor_z, check_hit corrects round hitboxes with it (001FBE)
field object 77 floor_type u8          # byte 0 of floor_types for the block's type (+12) (find_floor); the player and the rings test it (7 in 01E4ED, 0xD in 002CEC)
field object 7A floor_attribute u16 floor_attribute_record@floor_types    # word 2 of floor_types for the block's type (find_floor); the player tests it (4, 5 in 00E488/002CEC)
field object 7C hitbox_offset_x s8     # box hitboxes start at x + this (001E55, 0018D8, 0022DA)
field object 7D hitbox_offset_y s8     # box hitboxes start at y + this (001E82, 0018F3, 0022F5)
field object 7E health s8              # enemies: 00E488 subtracts the attacking player's strength (player block 72) when it hits them, they die at 0 (00F8E1), the sturdiest start at 0x7F (00EED2, 00F1F1); players: their rings (00E488 adds ring pickups, hits take 4 or 8 off in 002CEC, at 8 or less some hits put the player out with flags bit 10; starts at 20E66A: 0x10 in the reference run)
# 7F-9F are each object type's own variables. Where symbols.txt names them for a family of functions
# ("scoped object" lines) the C reads them by those names; elsewhere by these, named after their offset
# like the generic slots of other decompilations (var_80: this object type's variable at 0x80)
field object 7F var_7F u8
field object 80 var_80 u8
field object 81 var_81 u8
field object 82 var_82 u16
field object 84 var_84 u16
field object 86 var_86 u16
field object 88 draw_depth u16  # The depth an object others draw relative to keeps here: every object a player or a crawler stands on, and every one a player falls over or drops from (platform 74, touched_by 6A), keeps its draw depth (screen y + depth offset) at 88, and the player states read it (states.c: 16 reads, platform/touched_by's 88 -1 / +1; check_player_floor_edge), as do crawler_head_update/crawler_segment_update (platform's 88 - F), icicle_update (its platform piece's + 1), icicle_buried_part_draw / icicle_cracks_spread / icicle_shadow_follow (the icicle's), rimmed_sinkhole_edge_zone_update (the hole's) and saw_sparks_update (the blade's + 1); lava_rock, crumbling_floor, falling_grate, river_water, sand_block, rope_bridge_plank, collapsing_bridge_plank, ice_floor_block, ice_platform_piece, icicle_update, river_raft_update, saw_blade, sinkhole, rimmed_sinkhole and clipped_copy_sprite all name their 88 draw_depth. Not a depth, read through another object's pointer (no family yet, N1): fire_vent_burst_animate's AS8 store of FF (the vent's burst_state) and saw_sparks_update's test of the blade's parent's 88 (the rising saw's base_speed: drawn while it moves). Families name 88 their own way in their own code (fire_front base_speed...)
field object 8A var_8A u16
field object 8C var_8C u16
field object 8E var_8E u8
field object 8F var_8F u8
field object 90 var_90 u16
field object 92 spawn_arg_1 u16          # the stage lists' objects get the record's next-to-last word here (spawn_objects_by_type)
field object 94 spawn_arg_2 u16          # ... and its last
field object 96 var_96 u16
field object 98 var_98 u16
field object 99 var_99 u8
field object 9C next_handler u32         # spawn_objects stores the creator's return address here; the objects 083B14 restarts keep their next handler

# ======== the object list and the two pools ========
# Pool 1: 0x80 blocks of 0xA0 bytes at 0x200000-0x204FFF (stack free_object_stack, 16-bit addresses).
# Pool 2: 0xFF blocks of 0x30 bytes at 0x205000-0x207FCF (stack free_object_stack_2): sprite-only pieces
# (shadows, chain parts) that hang from a pool 1 object through child (28) and are never in the list.
# The list is circular through previous/next; run_objects starts at last_object's next (the first) and
# ends with last_object. New objects go at the end, so they run in the frame they are created.
0991B3  func  reset_objects            # RENAME of reset_objects: "bsr 991EE; bsr 99317; br 991C1" empties the list and both pools, then run_objects finds object_count 0 and only reloads R21; called on game mode changes (000243, 0002D4, 000446, 001D0F, 09C94A, 09CC03), never every frame (the frame routine 0000DF calls run_objects itself)
0991EE  func  reset_object_list        # first/last_object_address = 0x200000, free_object_stack = 0x80 then 0x0000, 0x00A0 ... 0x4F60, object_count = 0
099317  func  reset_object_pool_2      # free_object_stack_2 = 0xFF then 0x5000, 0x5030 ... (0x30-byte blocks)
099218  func  take_free_object         # pops the free stack into R11 (0x200000 | entry) without linking it (08A4ED, 08A9DC, 08C6E1, 08D32D)
099229  func  allocate_object_or_start_list   # allocate_object, or when object_count is 0: pop one and make it first and last, linked to itself (08F22D, 001D07, 096E24)
099256  func  link_object              # the tail of allocate_object: R11 goes between last_object and first_object (previous/next), becomes last_object, object_count + 1
0992A4  func  delete_current_object    # unlinks object_cursor (R23), moves R23 back to the previous object so run_objects goes on with the right next one, R20 = the freed block, then push_free_object (216 callers: "this object is done")
0992D3  func  push_free_object         # free_object_stack + 1, stores R20 on top
0992E4  func  delete_object            # the same for the object in R0 (unlink, fix first/last, push on the free stack)
099369  func  free_object_2            # pushes R0 back on free_object_stack_2 (pool 2 blocks are never linked)
01F1D7  func  allocate_object_outside_loop   # reloads R21/R22/R24 from 20E900 and first/last_object_address, then allocate_object: the spawners that run from the game mode code use it
01F1EA  func  delete_object_outside_loop     # the same around delete_object, storing first/last back (090CFA; unreached in the tests)
08DE6E  func  init_object              # init_object_fields with R12 = 0: every field
08DE74  func  init_object_2            # R12 = 1: only 00-2F, the size of a pool 2 block

# ======== spawning from the stage lists ========

08DC63  func  spawn_objects_by_type    # stage_spawns_by_type: object_types[type] gives spawn_count (+0) and the handler (+4); the record's words go to projected_x, projected_y, z (not x/y: unproject_object computes those), 92 and 94; a record is dropped when the pools are full

01E37E  func  spawn_ring_rows          # stage_template_spawns: count objects from stage_object_templates (all six are rings: frame 5E70, kind 3) along a line (dx, dy), each with a pool 2 shadow (frame 5D90) as child; z = floor_z - template word 8 (kept in 82)
091220  func  spawn_object_groups      # the list at object_group_spawns: type 0/2/6 records make groups from stage_object_records (093269); types 1/8, 3, 4, 5, 7 call 0916F1, 091F1B, 087EDE, 089EB0, 08CC66
09383A  func  spawn_object_groups_2    # stage_record_spawns: groups from stage_object_records_2 (093F59); types 1/4 call 0916F1
0973B4  func  timed_spawner_run        # handler: flags byte 0 = started, flags word 2 counts frames, byte 61 = next entry of timed_spawns; spawns each handler (offset from 0973B4) when its frame comes, deletes itself at FFFF
01C458  func  run_timed_spawns_2       # one entry of timed_spawns_2 for the calling object (61 = entry, flags word 2 = frames)
01D328  func  run_timed_spawns_3       # one entry of timed_spawns_3 (deletes the object at FFFF)
001D07  func  reset_objects_from_list  # reset_objects, then one object per handler of the list at 20F0EA (count, handlers) with allocate_object_or_start_list/allocate_object; 291F becomes 28D1/28DB from the player block's state (20F0EC walks the player blocks, + 0x200 each)
001CFD  func  start_player_objects     # reset_objects_from_list with player_objects (002405)

# ======== drawing: depth buckets and the sprite list ========
# Handlers queue what they want drawn into 256 depth buckets (sprite_buckets, linked through
# draw_next). After run_objects the frame routine 0000DF calls build_sprite_list, which walks the
# buckets from the last (FF) to the first (0) writing one sprite entry per object into the sprite RAM
# back buffer, and draw_queued_strings, which adds the text and the end command. The bucket is
# FF - clamp(depth + 0x10, 0, 0xFE): the lower an object is on screen, the later it goes out and the
# more it covers. Two buffers in sprite RAM (400020 and 404000); entry 1 (400010) is a jump that the
# VBLANK hook points at the finished one (with the global offset = screen centre, 70/A0).
099F2D  func  init_sprites             # sprite_flip from 20F618 and 500006-50000C from sprite_control_init, entries 0-1 from sprite_list_header, back buffer 400020, end marks at 400020/402010/404000/405FF0, vblank_hook, sprite_frames = 0x130000, then clear_sprite_buckets (the code from 099F35 and from 099F3B is init_sprites_from_frame_wait and init_sprite_hardware: the unused init_sprites_without_swaps and init_sprites_swapping_every_frame branch there)
elements sprite_control_settings u8      # sprite_control_init's bytes: init_sprite_hardware copies them to the sprite control registers 500006-50000C ("movz.bh [R10+], [R11+]" 099F50, 4 times); census ROM 09A6B2-09A6B5 (00 01 02 00)
099FA6  func  clear_sprite_buckets     # sprite_buckets_end = FFFF, each of the 256 buckets = its own address (empty)
099FBC  func  queue_sprite             # depth = screen_y, then queue_sprite_at_depth (65 callers)
099FC0  func  queue_sprite_at_depth    # R1 = depth: bucket FF - clamp(R1 + 0x10, 0, 0xFE), push R20 there through draw_next (145 callers)
099FF9  func  queue_sprite_in_layer    # bucket = low byte of sprite_layer (HUD and overlays)
09A012  func  queue_sprite_on_top      # bucket 0, drawn last
09A015  func  queue_sprite_in_bucket   # bucket = R0 (011EAB queues its shadow in 0xFF: drawn first, under everything)
09A02A  func  queue_sprite_at_floor    # depth = (projected_y + floor_z) >> 16 - view_y: sorts by the ground point under the object (rings, objects in the air)
09A074  func  queue_sprite_at_previous_floor   # the same with previous_floor_z
09A163  func  queue_sprite_at_previous_floor_2 # identical to 09A074 but leaves the bucket in R10 (unreached)
09A0BE  func  queue_sprite_at_base     # depth = screen_y - sprite_offset_y (the player, 002CEC)
09A102  func  depth_to_bucket          # R0 = FF - clamp(R1 + 0x10, 0, 0xFE), nothing queued
09A27B  func  build_sprite_list        # walks the buckets from 20FC00 down to 20FA02 writing entries from sprite_list_start (R19), emptying each bucket; the mode comes from sprite_flags bits 15/14/12 (jump table at 9A2E0); R19 ends after the last entry
09A1E9  func  swap_sprite_buffers      # vblank_hook: only when sprite_list_ready (then clears it): sprite_buffer_flip += 4, back buffer low word and the entry 1 jump (A002 / A400) from sprite_buffer_swaps; reads sprite_status (from the second += 2 on it is swap_sprite_buffers_now, which it falls into)
08E8AE  func  queue_string             # adds a text record (x, y, palette, scale, string pointer) to string_queue; R5 = 0 takes the 4 words from [R0] and the string after them; ignored when 43 are queued
08E8A6  func  queue_string_record      # queue_string with R5 = 0 (records like the "GAME OVER" one at 0025D0: 58, 68, 8440, 0200, text)
08E8AB  func  queue_string_at          # queue_string with R5 = 1: R0-R3 = x, y, palette, scale, R4 = the string
08E8F8  func  draw_queued_strings      # after build_sprite_list (R19): one entry (flags 000A, scaled by the record) per character through text_frames, then sprite_list_end_command; empties string_queue
20F008  var   sprite_list_ready  u8    # wait_for_frame sets it to FF when the frame's work is done; swap_sprite_buffers swaps (and clears it) only when it is set
20F100  var   vblank_hook  u32         # irq_vblank_end calls it ("jsr [7100[R25]]" at 09F566); init_sprites stores swap_sprite_buffers
20F106  var   sprite_buffer_flip  u16  # +4 at every swap; bit 2 picks the half (wait_for_frame keeps only bit 2)
20F108  var   sprite_back_buffer  u32  # sprite RAM address of the buffer the game fills next: 400020 or 404000 (swap_sprite_buffers rewrites its low word)
20F10C  var   sprite_list_start  u32   # wait_for_frame copies sprite_back_buffer's low word into it every frame; build_sprite_list starts writing there
20F110  var   sprite_list_end_command  u16   # FFFF (command 3, end of list), written after the last entry by draw_queued_strings
20F112  var   sprite_frames  u32 rom       # 0x130000: sprite_frame_records, the base sprite_frame points into (09A27B, 08E8F8, 0953BF)
20FA00  var   sprite_buckets_end  u16  # FFFF below the first bucket: build_sprite_list stops when a bucket holds a value above its own address
20FA02  var   sprite_buckets  u16      # 256 list heads, linked through draw_next; an empty bucket holds its own address
20C800  var   string_count  s16        # strings queued this frame (queue_string adds, draw_queued_strings empties)
20C802  var   string_queue  u16        # 12-byte records: x, y, palette, scale, u32 string pointer
130000  data  sprite_frame_records     # 4 words per frame: width in pixels, height (low byte) and address bits (high byte), bank bits, address low
09A6B2  data  sprite_control_init      # init_sprites: 4 bytes for 500006-50000C (0, 1, 2, 0)
09A6B6  data  sprite_list_header       # init_sprites: entry 0 (7000: clip to 0-13F x 0-DF, no exclusion) and entry 1 (offset 70/A0)
09A6CC  table sprite_buffer_swaps  sprite_buffer_swap # swap_sprite_buffers: (back buffer low word, entry 1 jump) at +0 (4000, A002) and +8 (0020, A400)
struct sprite_buffer_swap 4 rom            # a sprite_buffer_swaps record, by sprite_buffer_flip & 6 (swap_sprite_buffers_now "movea.h 9A6CC[PC](R0), R0" 09A20B: x 2): "mov.h [R0+], 7108[R25]" (09A211), "mov.h [R0], 400010" (09A217); census ROM 09A6CC-09A6DB (4000 A002, 4000 A201, 0020 A400, 0020 A5FF)
field sprite_buffer_swap 00 back_buffer_offset u16  # into sprite_back_buffer_offset: the buffer the game fills next (4000 or 0020)
field sprite_buffer_swap 02 list_jump u16  # into sprite_list_jump (entry 1 of the sprite list): the jump to the list just built
500002  io    sprite_status  u8        # swap_sprite_buffers reads it ("test.b 500002"); MAME: 1 normal, 2 overdraw
500004  io    sprite_flip  u8          # init_sprites writes 20F618 into it, 099552 the flip bits (MAME: D1 vertical, D0 horizontal)
50000C  io    sprite_wide_screen  u8   # 099552 writes bit 0 of its argument (MAME: 1 = 416 pixels wide, 0 = 320)

# ======== projection, camera and movement helpers ========
# 2:1 isometric view: x/y (16.16) are the ground plane, z is the height with larger values lower on
# screen (gravity adds to speed_z). Screen x grows with x + y, screen y with y - x and with z.
00C4DC  func  project_object           # projected_x/projected_y from x and y (0xB5/256 = cos 45 degrees), then update_screen_position (125 callers)

08E014  func  update_screen_position_no_offset   # the same without the sprite offsets

08DFBD  func  move_object_projected    # 88 += speed_x (projected_x takes the whole pixels from 8A), projected_y += speed_y, z += speed_z, then unproject_object (34 callers, the enemies)
08E037  func  move_object_projected_no_floor   # the same without unproject_object/find_floor (unreached)
00C53E  func  project_point            # R7/R8 = x/y, R9 = z: screen position of a point (R7 = x, R1/R8 = y) through point_to_screen
00C564  func  point_to_screen          # R0 = projected x, R1 + R9 = projected y + z: subtracts view_x/view_y
00C57C  func  project_object_2         # project_object, but once 20E435 reaches A5F0 screen_y uses the player block's DE instead of view_y (unreached)
00C453  func  set_speed_from_direction # speed_x = sine[direction] * speed >> 6, speed_y = -cosine[direction] * speed >> 6 (speed's high word)
00C4AD  func  set_speed_from_player_speed  # the same with the player block's 66 as the speed

# ======== collisions between objects ========
# Objects put themselves in lists while they run; the stage's mode routine (095177, also 000652 and
# 09492F) tests the lists in the next frame before run_objects (check_zones, check_hits, check_walls,
# check_platforms), sets flags bits and partner fields on both objects of each pair, and empties the
# lists. Lists are 16-bit addresses ending with FFFF.
20F07E  var   hitter_list  u16 object         # objects that test themselves against every touchable object and each other: the players (00B5BA) and 011EAB; through hit_list_next
20F080  var   touchable_list  u16 object      # objects the hitters can touch (rings, enemies, items: 77 handlers call add_to_touchable_list)
20F016  anchor  hitter_list     68             # check_zones starts its walk of the hitter list here: an object at 20F016 would have hitter_list as its hit_list_next (68)
20F018  anchor  touchable_list  68             # check_hits' first 'previous' of the touchable list: an object at 20F018 would have touchable_list as its hit_list_next
20E5F0  var   zone_list  u16 object           # objects whose box the hitters' x/y is tested against (check_zones; 010AD7, 080372, 082ED3...)
20F090  var   rider_list  u16 object          # objects that can stand on platforms and enter areas (the players, rings...); through platform_list_next
20F092  var   platform_list  u16 object       # platforms (085F80, 087FA5, 08815E...)
0020A5  func  add_to_hitter_list       # pushes R20 on hitter_list; clears flags bits 2 and 27
0020C2  func  add_to_touchable_list    # pushes R20 on touchable_list; clears flags bits 2 and 6
001956  func  add_to_zone_list         # pushes R20 on zone_list; clears flags bit 27
0020DB  func  add_to_rider_list        # pushes R20 on rider_list; clears flags bits 3 and 5
0020F4  func  add_to_platform_list     # pushes R20 on platform_list; clears flags bit 3
001DDD  func  check_hits               # every hitter against the hitters after it and, if it is not touched yet, against touchable_list; empties both lists
001E33  func  check_hit                # R17 against the list from R10: skips pairs where both kinds are 0-2; in x/y box/box, box/round (the round one as a square of its radius), point/box or circle/circle (radii summed, slope-corrected); then the heights; a hit sets flags bit 2 on both, touched_by to each other, 6C = a coordinate from the test (R2)
0018B6  func  check_zones              # every hitter whose x/y is inside a zone object's box with the heights overlapping: flags bit 27 on both, anchor_x = each other; empties zone_list
002108  func  check_platforms          # every rider whose x/y is inside a platform's box (no offsets): rider flags bit 3, platform fields of both; the platform also gets bit 3 when the rider's z is not above its floor_z (56), and the first time adds its 6F to the lists at 209400/209500 (sorted by 0021F9); empties both lists
00B5BA  func  add_player_to_lists      # add_to_hitter_list then add_to_rider_list (the player handlers)
00B5C6  func  remember_platform        # flags bit 4 = bit 3 (was on a platform)
01F0EF  func  check_left_screen        # R8 = -1 once an object that has been on screen (flags bit 11) is out of it by 0x20; sets bit 11 while it is inside
01F141  func  check_left_screen_margin # the same with the margin in R1
01F18C  func  check_left_screen_margins   # margin R1 once seen, R2 before
01F091  func  is_off_screen            # R8 = -1 when screen_x + 0x20 >= 0x180 or screen_y + 0x20 >= 0x120
01F0BC  func  is_off_screen_margin     # the same with margins R1 (x) and R3 (y)

# ======== shadows and the rings the generic code makes ========
01EF99  func  draw_child_shadow        # puts the child (pool 2, frame 5D90) at the floor under the object (projected_y + floor_z, sprite offsets), palette 9FFE, or 87A0 every other frame when flags bit 4; queues it at its screen_y - 0x10 (behind the object)
01E709  func  scatter_rings            # R8 rings (at most 10) at the current object: kind 3, flags 0x204 (bit 9 for the first 0x1E frames), speed/direction/jump (random unless 20F0EA says so), a pool 2 shadow each, handler scattered_ring_wait
01E701  func  scatter_rings_random     # 20F0EA = 0: random direction, speed and jump for each ring (00F8E1, drop_rings)
01E6F7  func  scatter_rings_fixed      # 20F0EA = FFFF (0826CE; unreached)
01E85B  func  scattered_ring_wait      # handler: 7E counts down with flags bit 9 set, then scattered_ring_live
01E86E  func  scattered_ring_live      # handler: 80 counts 0x12C frames, then the ring shrinks away; touched: taken (sound 13, 01EA86, deleted with its shadow) unless the player is in state D/20 with C3 set
01E8C8  func  move_scattered_ring      # moves on x/y (steps back and turns round when the floor rises more than 8), gravity 0x6000, bounces keeping 3/4 of speed_z, animates; out of the screen (is_off_screen_margin 0x20/0x58) it switches to scattered_ring_vanish
01E9C1  func  scattered_ring_vanish    # handler: ring and shadow sprite_scale - 0x10 a frame, then deleted
01EEC2  func  next_random              # reads two words through the random number area at D80000 (position 20F0FC, moved on by each value); R3 = the result

# ======== players (from build/naming/players.txt) ========
# Naming proposals: THE PLAYERS (struct player, the player handlers and state machine, player globals)
# Format: symbols.txt syntax, one proposal per line, "# evidence" after it.
# Conventions used below: "p" is the player number (OBJECT->player, 0-2); "the object" is the player's object
# (struct player +14 points at it, the object's 9C points back at the block).
#
# ======== struct player (0x200 bytes from 0x208400, R18 = current_player) ========
field player 00 state u8                    # 002CEC jumps through the table at 002D3E (58 entries) and 002FF1 through 002FFC; values below
field player 01 facing u8                   # 16-way sprite direction: ((facing_angle + 0x20) >> 6) & 0xF (00BD2C); indexes every animation table by 2 x facing
field player 03 substate u8                 # step inside a state (AT8(unk_02, 1) in the C): states switch on it, reset to 0 on most state changes
field player 04 state_timer s16             # per-state countdown/counter: 0x3C on a ledge (state 5), 0x1E/0x14/6 hurt and bounce, 0x168 goal run, +1 in state 0x24
field player 06 control_lock u8             # frames the trackball is ignored: counts down in the normal states (002DEC); 00B90A runs only when 0; set 4/0xA after bounces, 0x10/0x7F/0xFF in scripted states
field player 07 jump_delay s8               # 00B60A: counts down, the button is only checked (00B62D) when it reaches 0; 1 after a jump, 2 after being pushed out of an object
field player 08 standing_started u8         # 0030AD: 0xFF the frame the standing animation starts (long first frame); frames then last 3, except 2 and 6
field player 09 is_joining u8               # 0xFF from the credit (states 0xB/0x23/0x24) until the join sequence 00E1A9 ends; 001D07 then starts the object at 0028DB
field player 0A trackball_x s16             # 00BDCE: this player's trackball_N_x (0x20F062 + 4p) & ~1, shifted left 8 (trace: dx 11 -> 0x0A00)
field player 0C trackball_y s16             # 00BDCE: the same from trackball_N_y (0x20F064 + 4p) (trace: dy -4 -> -0x400)
field player 0E invulnerable_timer s16      # 002CEC decrements it every frame and stops at -1; >= 0 ignores hazards (00E488); 600 while hurt, 120 after a hurt or a respawn; blinks via object 30 bit 29 (00B5DC)
field player 12 heading u16                 # angle (0-0x3FF) the player moves toward; turns toward target_heading at a limited rate (00BC50)
field player 14 object u16 object                  # 002808: the player's object (low 16 bits); 001A7F, 00BED5, 015F80, 0983FE read it
field player 1A last_hazard u16             # 00E488: object that last hurt the player; a hit from another object restarts the hurt substate
field player 1C scene_hop_z s32             # state 0x18 scene step 6: height added to z while the character hops in place (speed_z per character)
field player 20 ledge_pullback s16          # 00B361: trackball movement back toward the floor while teetering (state 5) or slipping (7); >= 0x10/0x14 recovers
field player 22 ledge_side s16              # 00B3AC: side of the floor block the player went off (0-3), 4 = still inside; -1 when unused
field player 24 slip_distance s32           # state 7: += speed every frame; ends the slide at 0x20000000 (0x8000000 on floor type 9)
field player 28 target_heading u16          # angle from the trackball (00BBEC, 00B2C0) or the autopilot path (00DCC5); heading follows it
field player 2C climb_remaining s16         # state 0xA: height left to the top of the wall (0 = climb over, table +6 = back at the bottom); state 0x27: the x that ends the climb (object 94)
field player 2E climb_from_top u8           # state 0xA: 0xFF when the player reached the wall at or above its top (climbs down; falls if it came jumping)
field player 2F hit_stop u8                 # 00E488 sets 3 when the jump takes the enemy's health to 0 (sturdy kinds excepted; otherwise the player bounces off); while nonzero the player does not move (002EF7)
field player 30 step_accumulator s32        # state 0xA: speed_y summed, +-4 climbs one step; state 0x27 (008AD2): speed summed in the high word, 0x400 = one step
field player 34 screen_x s32                # 16.16 screen x used when the code places the sprite directly: climbing, dying (0x16), scenes 0x18/0x1C, riding (0x27)
field player 36 screen_x_int s16        # the whole part of screen_x
field player 38 in_game s8                  # 1 while the player has a game going (credit used), 0 when out; 002953 respawns only when > 0
field player 3C skid_slowdown s32           # state 0xC: ground_speed / 8 (/32 on floor type 7), subtracted every frame
field player 40 skid_speed_slowdown s32     # state 0xC: object speed (6E) / 8 (/32 on floor type 7), subtracted every frame until 0
field player 46 free_turn_timer u8          # counts down in the normal states; while nonzero 00BC50 sets heading = target_heading at once (no skid)
field player 48 skid_dust_timer s8          # state 0xC: a dust puff (00A669) every 4 frames
field player 49 bounce_direction u8         # state 0xE: 0-3, picks the bounce animation (table 1139E8 + 6 x dir); set by 00C920/00E488 (as a 16-bit write that also hits 4A)
field player 4A bounce_speed_z s32          # state 0xE and 0x1D: the bounce animation advances a frame each time speed_z passes it; += bounce_step
field player 4E bounce_step s32             # state 0xE: step added to bounce_speed_z (0x34000, then 2/3 of the rebound)
field player 52 previous_state u8           # saved before a forced state (stage events, ledges, scenes) and restored by them
field player 53 ignore_screen_edges u8      # 00AD91 does not push the player back from the screen edges while set (only cleared, in 0029DF)
field player 5C path_pointer u32 player_path_step  # 00DCC5: current record of the autopilot path (ROM 115528): +0 speed, +2 x, +4 y, +6 flags (bit 0 jump), 8 bytes each
field player 64 ground_speed s32            # 16.16 speed along heading after the slope tables (00B90A, 00BD5F); 00C4AD turns it into speed_x/speed_y
field player 68 walk_cycle s16              # walking: += animation_speed >> 16 every frame; each 0x200 the walk animation steps and the pending movement is applied
field player 6A walk_pending_x s32          # state 1 at low speed: speed_x summed and added to x only on animation steps (002EB0)
field player 6E walk_pending_y s32          # the same for y
field player 72 attack_power s8             # set to 4 when a jump starts (constant in this build; sound 0x1F); subtracted from the enemy's health (object 7E) in 00E488
field player 75 joined_health_setting u8    # 002808: copy of health_setting at join; indexes the max health table 113EF2 (00E488)
field player 76 previous_x s32              # x before this frame's movement; restored when blocked (00B6AC, 00C920, 00E488)
field player 7A previous_y s32              # the same for y
field player 7E previous_z s32              # the same for z (height)
field player 84 screen_edge u16             # 00AD91: which screen edge (0-3) pushes the player back; indexes 113EE0 and 113CE7
field player 8A heading_snapped u16         # 00BD0B: heading rounded to 16 directions; object 24 gets it + 0x80
field player 94 push_x s16                  # 00DA9B: floor push (table 10E14C + 7A) or quicksand pull (00E488 kind 28); added to the trackball in 00B90A
field player 96 push_y s16                  # the same for y
field player 98 animation_speed s32         # smoothed trackball speed: 0 -> standing, < 0x200 walking (1), else running (0x13), > 0x4F0 running fast (0x14) (00B90A)
field player 9C holder u16 object.vine_bar  # state 0x15: the object (kind 8/10) holding the player; set in 00E488 (pointer typed: last_names.txt N1)
field player A0 pushed_out s8               # 00E488 kind 5/12/32/33: 0xFF while the player is stuck in a solid object and being pushed out
field player A1 push_out_delay s8           # 00E488: 0x1E frames against the same solid object before pushing out
field player A2 push_out_x s32              # 00CCB0: push-out speed toward the screen centre
field player A6 push_out_y s32              # the same for y
field player AA fall_draw_depth u16         # states 6-9: sprite sort key while falling into a pit (floor screen y, adjusted by floor block type)
field player AC jump_first_tile u16         # state 4: first sprite of the jump animation; gravity applies once the animation leaves it
field player B0 path_speed u16              # 00DCC5: speed of the current path record (0 = wait path_wait frames)
field player B2 path u8                     # 00DCC5: autopilot path being followed (0 = trackball control); the trackball is ignored while set
field player B4 mishap_flag u8              # 0xFF when hurt, falling into a pit, joining...; 001A7F turns any of them into 20E5A3 and clears all three
field player B5 saved_substate u8           # 002F46: substate kept when a floor type forces a new state
field player B6 facing_angle u16            # angle the sprite faces (from the trackball, 00BBEC); facing = 16-way version
field player B8 scene_step_seen u8          # states 0x18/0x19/0x1C/0x1E: last scene_step handled, so each step runs its setup once
field player B9 path_request u8             # path to start (00DCC5 copies it into path): 0x14 intro run, 5, 0xE, 0x2F, 0x4D, 0x50, 0x53, exit paths
field player BA scene_zoom s32              # states 0x18/0x1C: drives the object's zoom (08) in the stage scenes
field player BE hud_blink_timer s8          # 00AD0D: 0x1E frames per blink of the player's HUD message
field player BF hud_blink_on u8             # 00AD0D: toggles; draws or erases the message
field player C0 path_wait s16               # 00DCC5: frames to wait at a path record with speed 0
field player C2 entry_status u8             # 002BC5/00D2BA: 0xFF playing, 0x81 dropping in from above, 0x82 waiting for the stage; copied to player_status[p]
field player C3 hurt_contact_delay s8       # states 0xD/0x20: frames before 00E488 checks contacts again (2 after a hit, 0xA/0x78 at start)
field player C4 speed_scale u16             # 00D2A7: target speed x speed_scale / 16 when nonzero; the pacing object 0843D5 sets 0xD on one player by position
field player C6 last_damaged u16            # 00E488: enemy last hit by the jump; the same enemy is not hit twice in a row
field player C8 escape_progress s32         # trackball shaking toward breaking free: states 0x1D (007834), 0x25 step 12, 0x32
field player CC draw_depth u16              # sprite sort key passed to 099FC0 (floor screen y): 0030AD, 0032DD, 00D22E
field player CE side_step_accumulator s32   # state 0xA: speed_x summed, +-2 moves one step along the wall
field player D2 saved_screen_x s32          # state 0xA: screen_x before the last step, restored by 00E488 when the step is blocked
field player D6 saved_screen_y s32          # state 0xA: object 2C before the last step
field player DA saved_climb_remaining u16   # state 0xA: climb_remaining before the last step
field player DC goal_step u8                # state 0x21 (stage exit): 0 start the exit path, 1 walking it, 2 done
field player DD effect_spawned u8           # state 0x22: the effect (084BBA type 0xB) was already started
field player E0 last_wall u16               # 00B6AC: wall (object 78, list 20F0AE) that last pushed the player back
field player E2 wall_timer s8               # 00B6AC: 0x1E frames of being pushed back by the same wall
field player E3 drift_anim_step u8          # 0096F1: animation step while carried by the scroll (states 0x25/0x26)
field player E4 continue_frames s8          # state 0x23: frames of the current second (60; the button jumps to the next)
field player E5 continue_seconds s8         # state 0x23: 9 down to 0, drawn by 099A57; at 0 the game is over (0x2E)
field player EA sequence_step u8            # step of the long scripted states 0x25 and 0x31 (they do not use substate)
field player EB ledge_direction s8          # when ledge_side is 4: side from the floor block's slope (0-3); 00D7E8, states 5/9/0x33

#
# Player states (field player 00). Main table at 002D3E (002CEC), animation table at 002FFC (002FF1); the
# code labels below name each state's entry.
#   00 standing (00B90A: no input)                 01 walking (animation_speed below 0x200)
#   02 falling to a lower floor (00C920)            03 inactive: the handler returns at once (no setter found)
#   04 jumping, the attack (button, 00B62D)         05 teetering at a pit edge (slow): pull back to recover, else 06
#   06 falling off the edge into the pit            07 over an edge at speed or jumping into a pit: slides, hangs on; pull back to climb up, else 08
#   08 dropping from the edge into the pit          09 falling into a pit from the air (00B465)
#   0A climbing a wall (floor type 2)               0B not playing: waits for a credit and the start button
#   0C skidding (turn of 90 degrees or more at speed, 00BC50)  0D hurt (-4 health, knocked back, invulnerable)
#   0E bouncing off a wall or an object at speed    0F launched by a bumper (kinds 6/7), bouncing to a stop
#   10 the same as 0F, from floor type 3            11, 12 the same code as 0F (no setter found)
#   13 running                                      14 running fast (animation_speed above 0x4F0)
#   15 held by an object (kind 8/10 caught while jumping) until it lets go
#   16 dying (health 0): flies off the screen, then 0x23
#   17 hopping (floor type 6, or released by a holder)
#   18 stage 0 / stage 5 scene (00D026): paths, poses and zoom by scene_step
#   19 thrown by the game mode 0x0D event (stage 8), by scene_step
#   1A inactive (returns at once)                   1B one 65-frame animation, then standing (no setter found)
#   1C opening scene of the first stage (game mode 0x10, 00D2BA)
#   1D stuck in an object (kind 17): shake the trackball to escape
#   1E game intro (mode 1): waits for its character's turn (intro_character), then runs path 0x14
#   1F blown away (kinds 19, 34): off the bottom of the screen, -8 health
#   20 hurt and tumbling (kinds 20, 23, deep floor type 0xD; -4 health)
#   21 stage exit (goal line reached, 00D026): walks the exit path
#   22 in a kind 0x16 zone (moves as usual)         23 continue countdown (9 to 0)
#   24 out of the game: message, then 0x0B         25 floor type 8 sequence (sequence_step; shake to escape at step 12)
#   26 pulled by scene_object (20E5F5), thrown, carried with the scroll, then skids
#   27 climbing along an object (kind 26) hand over hand to an x
#   28 swept away in a swirl (kind 30): up off the screen, -8 health
#   29 tripped (kind 31): a hop, then hurt          2A walking in along the stage's entry path (00CFCA)
#   2B game mode 0x18 (stage 0x11, the last): waits for 20E64F (object 01DDF4), +200 rings, then continue countdown
#   2C stuck on a kind 35 object, shake to escape (code not run in the scenarios)
#   2D held by an object of kind 37 (returns at once)
#   2E game over: ranking initials if the rings qualify (08EAC9, 08EC87)
#   2F stunned (kind 18; -4 health, 60 frames)
#   30 caught by scene_object, dropped and hurt (game mode 0x19, stage 0x10)
#   31 carried off (game mode 0x1A, stage 8; sequence_step) to player_carriers[p], then 0x32
#   32 trapped: shake the trackball to break free
#   33 sinking (floor block types 0x22/0x26): -8 health
#   34 choosing a character (game mode 0x1B, or after joining: 00E1A9)
#   35 riding (game mode 0x1C, stage 8)             36 knocked off the stage (kind 38): -8 health
#   37 slot disabled (player 3 with a two-player setting, 002808)
#   38 stage 0xB sequence (00D637): paths, a pose, waits, runs off
#   39 game mode 0x20 ("YOU FAILED"): continue countdown when 20E664 is set
