# ======== stages (from build/naming/stages.txt) ========
# Stages: proposals from the stages helper (symbols.txt syntax, one per line, "# evidence")
# The object sections at the end come from six helpers this helper ran (one per address range), checked
# and adjusted here (names aligned with objects.txt/system.txt/players.txt, game modes written in hex).
#
# How the stage system works (summary; details in the comments below):
# - stage (20F06E) selects 19 slots. Writing cleared_stages makes the protection device set the stage from
#   the order table at 002639 (cleared 0..14 -> 07 06 05 08 09 0A 03 04 10 0C 0D 0E 0F 0B 11) and clear
#   stage_init_flags (20F0BC-20F0BF; MAME: CURRENT_LEVEL_STATUS); the program never writes stage for that.
#   Stage select (game mode 8, slots 00-11) writes stage_select_cleared_values[stage], so its slots 00, 01
#   and 02 come back as 05, 07 and 07 (checked with s32ref: stage_00 and stage_05 both play stage 5,
#   stage_01/_02/_07 all play stage 7). Slot 00 is entered only from inside stage 5: run_stage_05_switch
#   (game mode 0x0A) sets scroll_position 5E5A and stage 0. Slots 01, 02, 12 are never reached. Stage 6
#   (the first after a new game) has no play: its only event is game mode 0x10 (update_stage_06_background),
#   which ends in mode 2.
# - Shared data (per-stage offsets that coincide): stage 7 (the attract demo of game mode 1) reuses stage 3's
#   map (floors, block map, path); 6 reuses 5's; 0E reuses 0C's and 0F reuses 0D's map, path, goal and
#   restart points (only their spawn lists differ); 01, 02, 11 and 12 point at copies of other stages' tables.
#   Stage 9 is the only one whose scroll script starts in mode 0 (it scrolls by itself); the others follow
#   the players (mode 7).
# - game mode 2 = start_stage; game mode 3 = the stage's frame (update_scroll, update_stage_tile_layers,
#   find_nearby_floor_blocks, update_restart_point, the six spawners, check_stage_clear, run_stage_events).
#   run_stage_events switches game_mode to the stage's scripted modes (0x0A-0x1F) at scroll positions:
#   stage 3: 11, 16 at 1B80, 16 at 8610, 15 at A360; 4: 11, 0C; 5: 0A at 100; 6: 10; 8: 0D, 1A at 3100,
#   1C at 7A8D; 9: 13, 14 at 1800, 12 at 4C00; A, C: 11; B: 1F at F00; 10: 11, 19 at C80; 11: 18.
#   Game mode 0x11 opens the screen with update_screen_wipe. A stage ends when the players have walked their
#   exit path past the goal and goal_unlocked is set (an object of each stage sets it: the end machine, the
#   last icicle dropper, goal_unlocker_start...): check_stage_clear goes to 0x17 (stage clear banners), 0x1D
#   (ring tally), 4 (the island map), 2; stages B-F go to 0x1E (a fade straight into the next stage).
#   The only time limit is stage B's escape (game mode 0x1F: 20 seconds once escape_started is set).
# - The camera follows a path made of sections: per section a direction, an end position (in scroll units),
#   x/y limits, a speed and a scroll mode script. scroll_position counts the distance along the path and
#   keys everything: spawn lists, stage events, restart points, the goal.
# - Coordinates: objects have ground x/y (4C/50) and height z (40); project_object turns them into
#   projected coordinates (2A = (x+y)*0.707, 2C = (y-x)*0.354, isometric) and the screen position (0E/0C) is
#   projected - view (view_x/view_y follow the camera).
# - Collision with the map: the stage's floors are boxes (x/y ranges, height, slope, surface kind) in
#   floor_blocks; every frame find_nearby_floor_blocks lists the ones near the view and find_floor
#   gives an object its floor and height. Walls are objects (spawn_walls) that push the players back.
# - Stage objects come from six spawn lists keyed by scroll_position. Most hazards that follow the players
#   are "chasers": a path script of (position or coordinate, screen threshold, catch-up factor, speed,
#   delay) records; behind the threshold they move at max(speed, camera speed * factor >> 8), and they hold
#   back after a player mishap. chaser_object (20E5D4) is the current one (the stage 3 spiked roller, the
#   stage A tornado, the stage B/C fire front, the stage 10 propeller machine...); group leaders, the lava
#   flow, the icicle droppers and the geyser front move the same way.

# ======== Stage flow ========
00075E  func  start_stage                      # game mode 2: cleared_stages+1 (capped at 0E) unless stage_start_kind says not to, clears the stage state, start_stage_view, load_stage_map_pointers, load_stage_goal, find_nearby_floor_blocks, requests stage_start_sounds[stage], game_mode = 3
00196E  func  check_stage_clear                # scroll_position >= goal_scroll_position, 20E593 clear and stage_exit_started set: marks players_finished FF for the players not in play (player_status 0, 2, 3, 4, 82), then needs the u32 at 20E5E0 = FFFFFFFF (the three players_finished bytes and goal_unlocked: a 32-bit read across both variables): game_mode 0x17 (0x1E for stages 0B-0F)
001B74  func  continue_to_next_stage_slot      # when next_stage_slot_request is set: copies two floor_blocks records (stage_link_points), stage++ and load_stage_map_pointers; never runs (20E538 is only ever cleared)
001BED  func  load_stage_map_pointers          # current_restart_point = stage_restart_points[stage]; floor_blocks / floor_block_bounds pointers from 10B6CC / 10E29C
001C31  func  run_stage_events                 # stage_events[stage]: (scroll position, game mode) records; switches game_mode when scroll_position reaches one (within 100)
001CD6  func  update_restart_point             # advances current_restart_point (from itself on) to the first 8-byte record whose position is above scroll_position
001859  func  apply_stage_layer_blending       # stage_layer_blending[stage]: count, then (sprite blend mask, bit, offset from 208000, blend factor word) into the mixer shadows 20F1C0-20F1DE: the layer register gets the mask and the bit (12: blend with sprites, MAME segas32_v), 61004E the factor and enable bit 11
00CFF0  func  load_stage_goal                  # stage_goals[stage]: six u16 -> goal_scroll_position, goal_direction, goal_line, (the fourth is skipped: add.h #2, R12), goal_line_min, goal_line_max
00D026  func  check_player_reached_goal        # past goal_scroll_position and across the goal line (direction 0-3): player state 21 (stage 0: 18; stage 4 waits for goal_unlocked; stage 5 also on object 20E5CA's timer)
00CBAC  func  place_player_at_restart_point    # x/y from the current stage_restart_points record (three kinds), spread by player number; at a stage start (object flag 2000000, in a game) from the 6 bytes before the list
09A5F4  func  load_stage_palette               # stage_palettes[stage]: (source, count) copied to palette RAM at 60B800
016CE3  func  start_stage_view                 # stage != 11: init_stage_view (stage 11 only clears 20CA45)
0158E2  func  init_stage_view                  # display off; tile layer pages, zoom, mixer; the stage's four tile block sets; camera, scroll and section lists from the per-stage tables
01A959  func  move_camera_to_start_section     # load_camera_start_section, then update_camera_view
01A966  func  load_camera_start_section        # like init_stage_view's section setup but from section stage_start_section (attract demos start mid-stage)
016D09  func  run_stage_05_switch              # game mode 0x0A in stage 5: fade out, new tile layers, fade in, then scroll_position = 5E5A and stage = 0
0178AB  func  update_stage_06_background       # game mode 0x10 (stage 6's only event, the scene after a new game; a render shows a player running toward the screen ahead of a big machine with jaws): scripted tile layer and palette steps driven by stage_06_background_step
0968F4  func  update_screen_wipe               # moves four window edges (2090F0-2090FC) to their targets, writes them to 31FF80-31FF86; returns the done bits in R5 (game mode 0x11 waits for 0F)
016EC9  func  update_fade                      # mixer colour offsets 20F1D0-20F1D4 step from/to black or white; fade_kind < 0 when done

20F0BC  var   stage_init_flags      u32        # one bit per once-per-stage setup (bit 0 spawn_objects_by_handler, 2 spawn_ring_rows, 4 spawn_object_groups_2, 5 spawn_walls, 8 run_stage_events, 9 spawn_object_groups, B 001A7F, C 09532E, 6/D/E/10/11 game modes 8/1/17/1B/1D, F/12/13 players 1-3 in 0FFD90/00A85A): set on first run; the protection device clears it (and 20F0BE) with each write to cleared_stages (MAME: CURRENT_LEVEL_STATUS)

20E64C  var   goal_line_max         s16        # stage_goals+A  (TYPE: signed compares)
20F088  var   current_restart_point u32 restart_point  # pointer into stage_restart_points, moved by update_restart_point (8 bytes a point); read by place_player_at_restart_point ("mov.w 7088[R25], R10; add.w #2, R10" 00CBFF-00CC04, then [R10+])
20E5C6  var   stage_06_shake        u16        # update_stage_06_background step 7: counts down by 80, its high byte shakes the NBG0/NBG3 y scroll
20908F  var   stage_06_background_step  u8     # update_stage_06_background switches on it; game mode 0x10 sets 3 and 5
209088  var   fade_step             u8         # update_fade: 0 start, 1 stepping, 2 done
209089  var   fade_kind             s8         # update_fade: 0 to black, 1 from white, 2 from black, 3 to white; FF when done

20908C  var   stage_05_switch_step  s8         # run_stage_05_switch switches on it; FF when done  (TYPE: FF = done, tested signed 4 times, like fade_kind)

002639  table stage_order           u16        # stage per cleared_stages value: 07 06 05 08 09 0A 03 04 10 0C 0D 0E 0F 0B 11; the protection device reads it (MAME: big-endian at 263A, cleared 0 = 7), the program only copies it to stage_order_copy
00265B  table stage_select_cleared_values  u16 # game mode 8 writes [stage] to cleared_stages so that stage_order gives the stage back
002681  table stage_start_sounds    u8         # start_stage (and game mode 1) requests the sound [stage] with 09A5BC
002492  table stage_events          u16        # 19 offsets from 002492 to lists of (u16 scroll position, u8 game mode, u8 0); FFFF ends
struct stage_event 4 rom                  # a stage_events record: run_stage_events "cmp.h [R10], 6435[R25]" (bl: not yet), "sub.h [R10+], R0" (001C62), "mov.b [R10], 7061[R25]" (001C76), then stage_event_cursor + 4; census ROM 0024B8-002521 (0000 0D, 3100 1A, 7A8D 1C, FFFF...)
field stage_event 00 position u16         # the scroll_position that starts it (unsigned); FFFF ends the list
field stage_event 02 next_game_mode u8         # into game_mode (0A-1F; the byte after it is 0)
002520  table stage_link_points     u16        # 19 offsets from 002520 to two u16 offsets into floor_blocks (continue_to_next_stage_slot)
struct stage_link_point 4 rom             # the record stage_link_points[stage] leads to: two offsets into floor_blocks (continue_to_next_stage_slot "movz.hw [R10+], R0" 001B93, 001BC7), each + floor_blocks + 2 a floor_block; census ROM 002520-002523 (offset 0: every stage but 1 reads the table's own first words, 0000 0026) and 002546-002549 (stage 1: 02BC 0028)
field stage_link_point 00 from_block u16  # the block of this stage's floor_blocks the link leaves from (stage_link_from_block)
field stage_link_point 02 to_block u16    # the block of the next stage's floor_blocks it reaches (stage_link_to_block)
002694  table stage_layer_blending  u16        # 19 offsets from 002694: u8 count, then 6-byte records (mask, bit, RAM offset of the layer register shadow, blend factor word); used by stages 5, 9, 10
struct layer_blend_list 1 rom             # the head of a stage_layer_blending list: its record count (apply_stage_layer_blending "test.b [R10]" 00187D, "movz.bw [R10+], R8" 001881), the layer_blend_record records follow; census ROM 0026BA (2), 0026C7 (1), 0026CE (0)
field layer_blend_list 00 count u8
struct layer_blend_record 6 rom           # a record of a stage_layer_blending list: apply_stage_layer_blending reads it with [R10+] (001884 "movz.bh [R10+], R1", 001887 "movz.bw [R10+], R2", 00188A "movz.hw [R10+], R11", 0018A5 "or.h [R10+], 71DE[R25]"); census ROM 0026BB-0026CC (3E 0C 71C8 0100, 3E 0C 71C2 0100, 3B 0C 71C2 0200)
field layer_blend_record 00 blend_mask u8       # or.h into the layer shadow's low 6 bits (3E, 3B)
field layer_blend_record 01 layer_bit u8        # set1 in the layer shadow (C: blend with the sprites)
field layer_blend_record 02 shadow_offset u16   # the layer's mixer shadow, from the variables (71C8, 71C2: 20F1C8, 20F1C2)
field layer_blend_record 04 blend_factor u16    # or.h into mixer_blend (bits 8-11: 100, 200), with the enable bit 11
11419A  table stage_goals           u16        # 19 offsets from 11419A to six u16 (load_stage_goal); FFFF position = no goal (stages 0-2, 6, 7, 11, 12)
114B84  table stage_restart_points  u16        # 19 offsets from 114B84 to 8-byte records: u16 scroll position, u8 kind (0/2: u16 x, u16 y at +4; 1: u8 at +3 and two words through 00CC75); the 6 bytes before each list are the stage start (u16 shift that spreads the players, x, y)

# ======== Scrolling and the camera ========
# update_scroll runs every frame of the stage modes. The scroll mode script (stage_scroll_modes) says what
# the camera does; in modes 7/8 the speed follows the leading player (field 6E of his object).

0169CA  func  scroll_speeding_up               # scroll mode 4: scroll_ramp_speed + 1 every scroll_mode_duration frames up to scroll_speed, then mode 0; on the frame the ramp ends (0169FA) it goes on to set the camera velocity with the R3 its caller left (never ran in the scenarios)

# ======== More of the stage flow ========
# Game mode 0x0A (stage 5, update_stage_05_event, see the stage events helper): the stage runs until check_stage_clear
# would end it, then run_stage_05_switch (stage 0), Eggman's booth, a shake, explosions, then
# update_stage_00_exit_scene for 1B6 + 12C frames, then game mode 2 (stage 8).

01A6E1  func  escape_alarm_flash               # started by 095587 (game mode 0x1F, stage B): while 20E658 (the escape's seconds) is non-zero the green and blue colour offsets swing between 28 and 3F, sound 19 at each end

# ======== Draw list and object removal used by every stage object ========
# The draw list is 100 buckets at 20FA02 (one per screen line, 00-FE from the bottom); the sprite list
# builder walks them every frame, so an object is drawn only on the frames its handler adds it.

# ======== Stage 11 (the ending) and the scripted game modes ========
# (From the stage events helper: renders of s32ref dumps of stage_11 frames 3503-9400, stage_05, stage_06, stage_04, players_2, players_3 and ending.)
# How the ending works (game mode 0x18, stage 11; run_stage_events sets it at scroll 0):
# - update_ending runs every frame: build_ending_scene (step 0 sets up the screen: display off, layer
#   mixing, bitmap layer, vram scripts 171BEB 171C77 17280A 1725B2 1729B2 172A84, sound 94, colour offsets
#   20; step 1 spawns six objects), then floors, restart point, the spawners and the contact checks;
#   joining_closed is held at FF; game over (mode 7) if nobody is in play. start_stage_view clears
#   ending_scene_step for stage 11 instead of running init_stage_view.
# - First scene (frames 3503-4217 in stage_11): the three characters run toward the viewer on a road
#   (scale growing), a tower stands on the horizon behind them; the tower's own timed list
#   (timed_spawns_2, offsets from 01BFC4) fires burning debris arcs from its top, blasts at its base and
#   along the horizon, at 258 the tower collapses (frames 9B00-9B40), a huge explosion and a dust cloud,
#   at 26C the screen flashes to white (second colour offset set up to 1F); then
#   ending_first_scene_done makes the scene objects remove themselves.
# - Credits (4217-8080): ending_credits_fade_in comes back from white and starts the music; the credits
#   spawner (timed_spawns_3, offsets from 01C82F) starts the portrait (Sonic, Ray, Mighty), the name plate
#   with "STARRING" (then Eggman) and seven blocks that scroll up 1 pixel every 2 frames: the team logo
#   and STAFF title, DIRECTOR., PROGRAM., DESIGN., SOUND., VOICE ACTOR., SPECIAL THANKS. (role headings
#   as the renders show them); each block is a sprite plus second-pool parts from its part list.
# - Then the portrait window (clip rectangle 1) opens to the whole screen, fade to black, Eggman flies in
#   with a jet flame and a smoke trail, turns to the viewer, fade, a close-up of his machine flying away
#   into the distance ending in a twinkle, a circle opens (per-line window edges at 30A000/30A400, NBG2
#   pages set), and the three characters run across the screen; 0x78 frames later ending_finished lets the
#   players end the game (player state 2B), game over at 9364 (it prints the "GAME OVER" string record
#   0025D0 instead of 002342 when ending_finished is set).
# The objects keep their own counters in field 30 (byte 0 started, byte 1 a step or done flag, word 32 a
# frame counter) and 60-62 (indexes): per-object scratch, not named.

# ======== Stage 11: scene set-up ========
095177  func  update_ending                     # game mode 0x18 (stage 11): scene_step = FF, next_stage_slot_request 0, joining_closed FF, build_ending_scene, find_nearby_floor_blocks, update_restart_point, the spawners, the contact checks; game mode 7 when player_status is all 0
01BCC6  func  build_ending_scene                # switch on ending_scene_step: 0 display off, set_stage_layer_mixing, clear_sprite_buckets, clear_bitmap_layer, init_video_registers, load_stage_palette_set, queue_sound 94, colour offsets 20, 31FF02 |= 2F, pages and scroll shadows, zoom 200, clip rectangle 1 zero, six run_vram_script calls; 1 allocate_object_outside_loop x6: ending_tower_animate, ending_horizon_show, the three runners, ending_road_scroll; 2/3 nothing
01BF17  func  init_ending_scene_object          # clears field 30 (bytes 30, 31, word 32) of the new object R11 and sets ending_scene_step = 2
20CA45  var   ending_scene_step     u8          # build_ending_scene switches on it (0 screen, 1 objects, 2 done); init_ending_scene_object sets 2; start_stage_view clears it on stage 11
20CA44  var   ending_first_scene_done u8        # build_ending_scene clears it; ending_flash_to_white sets 1 at full white; ending_horizon_show, ending_dust_cloud_rise, ending_road_scroll and animate_ending_runner remove their objects then
20E64F  var   ending_finished       u8          # ending_sonic_run_across sets 1 after 0x78 frames (stage_11 run: frame 9239); start_stage clears it; player state 2B (002CEC, 002FF1) waits for it; game over (run_game_mode 000EE1) then queues the "GAME OVER" string record 0025D0 instead of calling 002342

# ======== Scripted game modes (run_stage_events, cases of run_game_mode) ========
# scene_step (20F0E2, players.txt) is the step of the scripted mode and scene_timer its timer;
# run_stage_events clears both when it switches the mode. Names event_XX_ use the game mode in hex, like
# system.txt's game_mode_event_XX labels. Three modes jump
# through tables of stubs indexed by scene_step (3-byte br for modes 0x0C and 0x0F, 2-byte br for 0x1C); the
# last entry of each table is the step-0 handler itself (09460F, 094888, 095116), reached only if the
# step ran past the end.
20F0E4  var   scene_timer           s16         # timer of the scripted game modes (counts up or down per mode), cleared by run_stage_events; also read by the players (002CEC/002FF1: stage 0 geyser ride while <= 90) and stage 6 objects (084169, 0841DA)

# Not named: 20E5BA (update_stage_05_event step 0 writes 0, nothing reads it) and 20E665 (game mode 0x1F
# step 0 writes 0, nothing reads it); 20E61A is shared (game mode 0x0D, 080160, 0803EB, 084778, 08481D,
# 0890DC, 08924E set or clear it; check_player_jump and player_steer stop the players while it is set):
# probably "player controls locked", left to the players helper.

# Game mode 0x0F: no stage event or code sets it (system.txt); its table at 094606 is dispatched from 0945CE
094606  func  game_mode_event_0f_case_00        # br event_0f_start
094609  func  game_mode_event_0f_case_01        # br event_0f_stop_scroll
09460C  func  game_mode_event_0f_case_02        # br event_0f_show_messages
09460F  func  event_0f_start                    # step 0 (and the table's entry 3): scene_timer 0, scroll mode 0 at speed 3, scene_step + 1
094626  func  event_0f_stop_scroll              # step 1: scene_timer + 1; from 3C scroll mode 1 (stop); at 78 event_0f_message_cursor = event_0f_messages, step 2
094659  func  event_0f_show_messages            # step 2: each record of event_0f_messages whose time has come: spawn_message_box(x, y, kind, frames); at 258 scroll mode 0 speed 5, game mode 3 (never run)
20E5B2  var   event_0f_message_cursor u32 event_0f_message       # pointer into event_0f_messages (event_0f_stop_scroll, event_0f_show_messages only)
0957FA  data  event_0f_messages                 # 10-byte records (time, x, y, message kind, frames): kinds 0-4 at 0, 78, FA, 136, 1EA; 7FFF ends (kinds 1-4 have sprite 0000 in message_box_kinds: unused leftovers)
struct event_0f_message A rom             # an event_0f_messages record: event_0f_show_messages "cmp.h [R10+], 70E4[R25]" + blt (094662: signed), then "mov.h [R10+]" into R5, R6, R7, R8 (09466A-094673) for spawn_message_box; census ROM 0957FA-095829 (0000 90 A0 0 78, 0078 B0 40 1 78, ..., 7FFF)
field event_0f_message 00 show_time s16   # the scene_timer that opens it; 7FFF ends
field event_0f_message 02 screen_x u16
field event_0f_message 04 screen_y u16
field event_0f_message 06 kind u16        # message_box_kinds index
field event_0f_message 08 frames u16      # how long the box shows

20E664  var   you_failed_done       u8          # set FF by game mode 0x20 at game_mode_timer 12C (after the "YOU FAILED" text at 78); player state 39 then starts the continue countdown

# ======== Stage objects 080072-0857E4: the chasers (spiked roller) and the objects of stages 3-7 ========
# Stage objects 080072-0857E4 (stage_spawns_by_handler handlers of stages 3-8, B-F and the chaser system)
# Renders: s32ref dumps of walk_03, walk_04, stage_06 (stages 7, 6, 5, 0), stage_0E, plus a frame renderer
# (sprite word + palette from a dump) for the sprites named below.
#
# How the chaser works (080160-080E75):
# - A spiked roller (sprites 5E20-5E60: a gear-shaped cross-section that turns over 9 frames) is built by
#   spiked_roller_start from spiked_roller_kinds[kind]: 5 parts side by side across the path (spacing and
#   direction from spiked_roller_layouts), each with handler spiked_roller_update; the first part is the
#   leader (field 86 of every part), the others copy its x or y (spiked_roller_follow_leader). The leader
#   becomes chaser_object. The parts are on the zone list: kind (field 47) 0C (solid: players are pushed
#   out) until its script starts moving, then 18 (players are hurt even while invulnerable; with flags
#   40000000 an attacking player bounces off along its direction: check_player_contacts), and a back zone
#   object (spawn_roller_back_zone) covers 200 units behind it so nobody can stay behind it.
# - spiked_roller_chase runs the leader's script (10-byte records keyed by scroll_position: screen
#   threshold, catch-up factor, base speed, wait frames): on screen past the threshold it moves at the base
#   speed, else at max(camera speed x factor / 100, base) (catch-up). chaser_speed is the speed (1/16 pixel);
#   the animation speed and a rumble sound (B) follow it. While a player drops in, has a mishap or no player
#   is in play it backs off (waits until it is off screen) for up to FF frames or 300 scroll units.
# - spiked_roller_events (by kind, keyed by scroll_position and a coordinate test) switch the leader to the
#   other states (field 80, jump table at 0803BB).
# - Stage 3: kind 0 at the start (players frozen until it moves; it falls off a ledge near 1B80), kind 1 bursts
#   out of a wall (game mode 0x16 holds the camera until it appears), kind 5 crashes into the machine at 8300
#   (wrecks it; its flame becomes the rising fire), kind 2 drops in near 9B00 and in the finale (game mode
#   0x15) sinks into the stone floor blocks, jumps and lands: the blocks fall and goal_unlocked is set.
#   Stage E: kind 4 rolls into the brick wall (brick_wall_wait bursts). Kind 3 is not spawned by any list.

# ======== Stone floor blocks that crumble at the stage 3 finale (nine at 9C00) ========
080072  func  stage_03_floor_block_start       # stage 3 list at 9C00 (3 x 3 at FA62-FAE9 / 0A79-0B8A, field 04 = kind 0-6): stage_03_floor_block_kinds[kind] gives sprite offsets 64/65, a depth offset (38) and the animation (6780/6770/6778/6798: stone blocks seen in the walk_03 finale renders), field 34 = which stage_03_floor_block_falls byte it waits for; z 0
0800FB  func  stage_03_floor_block_update      # waits until its stage_03_floor_block_falls byte is set, then falls (speed_z += 1000) playing its crumble animation once (6780 -> 6788 -> 6790 rubble); removed below screen y 158
082284  table  stage_03_floor_block_kinds stage_03_floor_block_kind  # by kind: offset from 082284 (to 64, 65, depth word, animation) and the fall flag index (kinds 0-2: 0, 3-6: 1)
20E5EE  var   stage_03_floor_block_falls u8    # [2]: stage_03_floor_block_start clears both; spiked_roller_sink_and_jump sets [0] when it starts sinking and [1] when it lands
struct stage_03_floor_block_kind 4 rom    # a record of stage_03_floor_block_kinds (082284), by kind 0-6: stage_03_floor_block_start "movea.w 82284[PC](R0), R10" (08007A), then [R10+]; census ROM 082284-08229F
field stage_03_floor_block_kind 00 shape u16  # "movz.hw [R10+], R11; add.w #82284, R11" (080080, 080083): offset from 082284 of the kind's stage_03_floor_block_shape: 1C, 28, 34, 40, 1C, 34, 34
field stage_03_floor_block_kind 02 fall_flag u16  # "mov.h [R10+], 34[R20]" (08009D): speed_x_fraction, which stage_03_floor_block_falls byte the block waits for: 0 for kinds 0-2, 1 for 3-6
struct stage_03_floor_block_shape 4 rom   # a block's sprite offsets and depth offset; its stage_03_floor_block_animation follows (080099 "mov.w R11, 48[R20]"): stage_03_floor_block_start reads it with [R11+] from 080083 "add.w #82284, R11"; census ROM 0822A0-0822CF (four, 12 bytes apart)
field stage_03_floor_block_shape 00 sprite_offset_x s8  # "mov.b [R11+], 64[R20]" (08008A): 0, 0, 0, 30
field stage_03_floor_block_shape 01 sprite_offset_y s8  # "mov.b [R11+], 65[R20]" (08008F): 0, 30, 30, 50
field stage_03_floor_block_shape 02 depth_offset u16  # "mov.h [R11+], 38[R20]" (080094): speed_y_fraction, taken from screen_y for the depth: 48, 48, 48, 18
struct stage_03_floor_block_animation 8 rom  # a block's animation, after its shape (stage_03_floor_block.animation, 48): last frame 2, then the block's sprite (6780, 6770, 6778, 6798) and its crumbling (6788, 6790; 67A0, 67A8 for the fourth); census ROM 0822A4-0822CF
field stage_03_floor_block_animation 00 last_frame u16  # 2 (animate_step reads it through the object's animation)
field stage_03_floor_block_animation 02 first_frame u16  # read in place: "mov.h 2[48[R20]], 4[R20]" (0800D9), the block's sprite before it falls

08078E  func  spiked_roller_follow_leader      # state 2 (the four other parts): copy the leader's (field 86) y and speed_y (or x and speed_x for directions 1/3), kind (47), height, box offsets, z and floors; follow its states 1 and 8; removed when the leader is in state 5

# ======== Stage objects 0857E5-08A16E: scenery and stages 3, 8, 9, A ========
# Stage objects 0857E5-08A16E (stages 3, 8, 9, A and the shared scenery/script objects), plus 08574A/08576F.
# Renders: s32ref dumps of stage_05 (stage 8),
# a stage 9 walk (gen.py --stage 09 --bias -1 -1 0.8 --seed 2: reaches the end of stage 9), walk_0A and
# walk_03, drawn with render.py and with a per-object renderer that rebuilds each object's sprite entries
# as build_sprite_list does (scratch s89a/objrender.py).
# Touch kinds (field 47) are read through the player's contact switch 00E488: 0x13 and 0x22 (when not
# invulnerable) blow the player away (state 1F), 0x14 hurts with a tumble (state 20), 9/0xC/0x28 hurt
# unless the player is attacking (then he bounces off), 0x1B makes him fall over an edge (state 7, no floor),
# 0x1C sinks him in quicksand (player 114 bit 2), 0x1D is a zone where edges drop at once (player 114 bit 1),
# 0x1E sweeps him away in a swirl (state 28), 0x1F trips him (state 29).
# "Chaser" movement (boulder, lava flow, bridge fire, icicle droppers, tornado, sand block leader): a script
# of records (scroll position and/or a coordinate to reach, then 84 = screen position threshold, 86 = speed
# factor, 88 = minimum speed, 90 = delay); speed = camera ground speed (00AFB3 -> 20E510, or 00B04D ->
# 20E572 with the floor slope) * 86 >> 8, at least 88, and only 88 once the object is past the threshold
# on screen. While no_player_in_play/player_mishap/player_dropping_in (20E599/20E5A3/20E596) are set the
# object holds back (8E = FF, minimum speed 0, threshold moved off screen) for up to 0x300 scroll units.

struct icicle_dropper_step C rom              # a step of an icicle_dropper_scripts script as the dropper walks it: its path (80) points at the step's scroll position; icicle_dropper_check_scroll_position reads +0 ("cmp.h [R10+], 6435[R25]" 0883F9), icicle_dropper_load_record the end test at +4 ("test.h 2[R10]" 088401, R10 = step + 2) and +2-+8 ([R10+] 08841A-08842C), path = the next step (+ C, 088432-088435). # ======== Stage objects 08A16E-08DC36 and the group rows 090E49-093E63: stages A-10 ========
# Stage objects 08A16E-08DC36 and row/group objects 090E49-093E63
#
# Common pattern of the chasers and group leaders below (fire front, biting head, rising saws, geyser front,
# waterfall, propeller machine, group_leader_move): a path script of entries (start scroll position or an
# x/y/z limit, a screen-x or screen-y threshold, a catch-up factor, a speed, a delay); while the object is on
# its side of the threshold it moves by the entry's speed, when it falls behind it moves by
# max(speed, camera speed * factor >> 8) (20E510 from 00AFB3, or 20E572 from 00B04D), so it keeps up with
# the screen. The step of the frame is left in chaser_speed (20E556). After a player mishap / a player dropping in / no
# player in play (player_mishap, player_dropping_in, no_player_in_play) it holds just off the screen edge for
# up to FF frames or 300 scroll units.
# Renders: s32ref dumps of tests/controls/walk_0C.txt (stages C, D, E), walk_0A.txt (stage A), and scratch
# copies of walk_0C with the stage poke changed to 10 and 08 and extended to 60000 frames (sb10/walk_10x.txt,
# sb10/walk_08x.txt); sprite frames drawn on their own with sb10/frames.py.

# Remaining names: proposals for what build/naming/unnamed.txt (12-10-2026) still lists.
# Syntax as in symbols.txt, one per line, each with "# evidence". Renders: s32ref dumps of
# tests/controls/attract.txt (frames 640-2200) drawn with the stages helper's render.py / frames.py.
#
# Characters: object field 47 (kind) of a player's object is the character it plays: 0 Sonic, 1 Ray,
# 2 Mighty (ranking records, character_name_sprites B728 SONIC / B738 RAY / B730 MIGHTY, the title).
#
# How the pieces named here work (summary; details in the comments):
# - SEGA logo and title (attract system_mode 3): attract_title runs run_title_screen every frame. Until
#   sega_logo_step reaches 7, run_sega_logo plays the SEGA logo (sprite 53D0 + 8n on a temporary second-pool
#   block: fade in from black, zoom in, 1E frames of animation, hold, fade out, 3C frames); then the title scene is
#   built once (title_scene_built): the emblem with Sonic rising out of it and Ray and Mighty popping
#   up (title_emblem_animate), a strip of land sliding in (title_land_slide), clouds drifting up-left and
#   growing (three groups, started by the timed spawner at 097419), a small craft crossing the sky with a
#   smoke trail, and a waving background (per-line scroll of NBG2, palette cycling). title_done after 258 frames.
# - Ranking (attract system_mode 2): start_ranking_display's object scrolls the "TOP 15" screen down,
#   holds 12C frames, then ranking_done. build_ranking_display makes 15 rows of 12 sprites (rank, initials,
#   portrait, name, four score digits, stage reached or ALL CLEAR) and the spinning "TOP15" title.
#   Records (8 bytes): rings (the score), character, stages reached (8 = ALL CLEAR), three letter codes, 0.
#   Letter codes: 00-19 a-z, 20-29 0-9, 2B space (ranking_letter_sprites).
# - Ranking entry (player state 2E): start_ranking_entry checks the player's rings against the lowest
#   record and sets up a static block (ranking_entry_blocks, outside the object pools) that
#   enter_ranking_initials runs: 3 letters chosen with the trackball, 20-second countdown, or OUT OF RANK!
# - Character select at the start of a game (game mode 0x1B, player state 34): start_character_chooser
#   makes the PLAYER SELECT heading with its countdown (character_select_countdown_update) and one chooser
#   per player: the character turns with the trackball x (character_chooser_turn), the button or the end of
#   character_select_timer confirms (character_chooser_confirm: voice, the character goes into the player
#   object's kind). Joining later (player_select_character): start_join_character_chooser shows a small
#   portrait with a 9-second countdown (join_character_chooser_update). characters_taken holds one bit per
#   character already playing.
# - Camera speed helpers for the chasers: compute_camera_ground_speed (flat) and
#   compute_camera_slope_speed (R8 = the floor slope factor) turn camera_velocity_x/_y into a ground speed
#   and direction, recomputed only when the velocity (or slope) changed.
# - Grey screen: update_grey_screen (every stage frame) greys the four tile layers (mixer 3E bits 1-4:
#   MAME's grayscale colour offset mode) while any player block's 9F is set, and some objects switch to
#   grey palettes (arrow_board_ride, crumbling_floor_update) or stop (group_leader_move, spiked_roller_chase). Nothing ever sets
#   player field 9F: the effect is dormant.
#
# Mirrors: rom_0FF08C/0FF08E and rom_0FFFCE-0FFFE0 are reads of 09F08C/09FFCE-09FFE0 through the 0FFxxx
# mirror (the code at 09Fxxx runs there). 09F08C is already rom_checksums: the names below are only needed if
# table reads are not folded to 09Fxxx (the decompiler does not fold them today).

# the C showed PLAYER(current_player)->unk_02 / unk_2A / unk_47 / unk_54 / unk_58 (and path_pointer,

field player 54 drift_turned_back u8        # state 26 (pulled, then carried with the scroll): 0 when the carried phase starts, FF once x >= CD0; then the drift turns to 300 (scroll_drift_direction) and the phase ends back at x <= 630 (player_state_pulled 008E31-008EB0, player_move_with_scroll)
field player 55 drift_done u8               # state 26: 0 at the carried phase's start, FF when it ends (with drift_turned_back, x <= 630); game mode 0x12 (094410) counts the players in play whose drift is not done

field player DE own_view_y u16              # project_object_2 and shadow_update subtract it instead of view_y once scroll_position >= A5F0 with per_player_view_mode; never written
field player E6 pull_angle u16              # state 26: 300 at the start, then a copy of scene_object's direction (24) every frame; the pull ends (player thrown) once it is 1D0 or less
field player E8 pull_start_distance u16     # state 26 start: (5D0 - x) >> 12
field player 12F sequence_bounced u8        # state 25 (floor type 8 sequence): 0 at steps 0/11, FF when the player lands and bounces (speed_z reversed and halved, speeds halved); game mode 0x14 tests it (094288)
field player 140 stage_b_path_done u8       # state 38 (stage B sequence): FF once the player has walked its path and stands facing direction 0; sliding_door_wait opens the door when every playing player has it; player_reset clears it
field player 14A hud_gauge_address u16      # gauge record +08 (sprite_scale, the address word of a sized frame): player_hud_init copies word +6 of frame 89E0's record

# ---------------- scoped object fields (7E-9F, per handler family) ----------------
# Format: "# scoped object FAMILY_PREFIX OFFSET NAME TYPE  # evidence". The names describe the fields of the
# object the family's code runs on (OBJECT(current_object)); inside these functions some lines touch other
# objects' fields at the same offsets (children being set up, the touched object, the parent), which these
# names do not describe: e.g. handle_rod_init sets its handles' 80-94, machine_fire_update its fireballs'
# 7F/96/9C, player_stuck_wait_release reads the holder's 80. Where a family's parts share the prefix with a
# different layout, the parts get a longer prefix that should win (burning_boulder_flame over
# burning_boulder, handle_rod_handle / handle_rod_post over handle_rod, group_leader_move / group_leader_hold,
# icicle_update / icicle_cracks / icicle_shadow instead of icicle, which would also take icicle_dropper).
# Most used families first. Not done (meanings change between the family's own handlers, or too little
# use): eel, snow_mound, sand_rock, rock_wall, spike_panel, saw_blade, opening_machine, flame_machine_*,
# eggman_scene, ember_emitter, crawler, centipede, whirlwind and the small effect objects.
#
# The chaser movement (fire front, biting head, sand block leader, propeller machine, waterfall, rising saws,
# lava flow, geyser front, bridge fire, machine fire, icicle droppers, burning boulder): one routine copied
# into each handler. A path script record gives a position or coordinate to reach, then (threshold, catch-up
# factor, base speed, wait); on its side of the threshold the object moves at the base speed, behind it at
# max(base, camera_ground_speed (or camera_slope_speed) x factor >> 8); chaser_speed gets the step. After a
# player mishap / a player dropping in / no player in play it holds back (threshold moved off screen, base
# speed 0) for FF frames or 300 scroll units.
# fire_front (fire_front_init, fire_front_chase): the chaser movement
scoped object fire_front 80 path u32 chase_step_with_limit  # next record of its path script (the record's words are loaded into 84/86/88/90 when its position or coordinate is reached)
scoped object fire_front 84 screen_threshold s16  # screen coordinate it compares its own with: on its side it moves at base_speed, behind it at max(base_speed, camera speed x catch_up_factor >> 8)
scoped object fire_front 86 catch_up_factor u16  # multiplies the camera's ground speed (>> 8) when it falls behind
scoped object fire_front 88 base_speed s16  # speed of the current record (chaser_speed when it is ahead)
scoped object fire_front 8A saved_threshold s16  # screen_threshold kept while holding back (a player mishap / dropping in / no player in play)
scoped object fire_front 8C saved_base_speed s16  # base_speed kept while holding back (base_speed is 0 meanwhile)
scoped object fire_front 8E holding_back u8  # FF while it holds back
scoped object fire_front 8F hold_timer u8  # FF frames of holding back at most (always FF without players in play)
scoped object fire_front 90 wait_timer s16  # frames of the record's wait: it does not move until 0
scoped object fire_front 92 hold_start_position u16  # scroll_position when it started holding back: it gives up after 300 units

struct sprite_palette_cycle 2 rom            # a palette cycle animate_sign steps through (animate_sign 80 palette_list): the last index, then the palettes, a word each; animate_sign 00CB29 "mov.w 80[R20], R10", 00CB2E "mov.h [R10+], R0" (last_index), 00CB51 "mov.h [R10](R1), 6[R20]" (palettes[R1] into sprite_palette); census ROM 08514D-085170 (sign_palette_lists: 5 0460-0490..., 3 84A0-84D0, 4 04E0-0500), 085CDF (fire_vent_glow_palettes), 085E7F (scenery_sprite_palettes), 08A686 (quicksand_palettes: D 1030-11D0)

elements sprite_cycle_palettes u16           # the palettes of a sprite_palette_cycle, after its last_index word: animate_sign reads palette_list + 2 + palette_index x 2 (00CB2E moves R10 past last_index, 00CB51 "mov.h [R10](R1), 6[R20]")

param spawn_message_box R5 screen_x
param spawn_message_box R6 screen_y
param spawn_message_box R7 kind
param spawn_message_box R8 frames
param convert_to_bcd R0 value
param copy_blocks R1 count
param copy_blocks R10 source
param copy_blocks R11 dest
param spawn_banner_sparkle R0 offset_x               # added to the banner's screen_x for the sparkle (0E); stage_clear_banner_reveal passes var_80, += 0x10 per sparkle
param apply_stage_layer_blending R2 layer_bit        # "set1 R2, [R11]": the bit set in the layer's mixer shadow (12: blend with sprites); out = the last record's bit, in = passed through when the stage has no records
param apply_stage_layer_blending R8 count            # loop counter (7 shadows, then the record count); always 0 on return
param check_stage_clear R8 count                     # dbr counter over the 3 players; in/out only because the early return leaves it alone
param check_stage_clear R10 finished_flag            # walks players_finished (20E5E0), set to FF for the players not in play
param check_stage_clear R11 status                   # walks player_status (20E590): 0, 82, 3, 4, 2 = not in play
param clear_player_blocks R8 count                   # dbr counter, 0x30 rounds of 0x20 bytes; always 0 on return
param update_grey_screen R3 count                    # dbe counter over the 3 player blocks (test of 9F); 0 when none is set
param update_player_summary R3 in_play_count         # number of player_status bytes with bit 7 set, stored to players_in_play (low byte)
param update_player_summary R8 count                 # dbr/dbne counter over the 3 players
param update_player_summary R10 cursor               # walks player_status (20E590), then the player blocks (208400 + 0x200), then player_status again
param update_player_summary R11 player_object        # mov.h 14[R10], R11: the player's object (test of its 30 bit A)
param continue_to_next_stage_slot R1 table_offset    # what load_stage_map_pointers hands back (offset in the bounds table); also the offset read from stage_link_points (folded in the C)
param continue_to_next_stage_slot R11 block          # points at the "from" and then the "to" floor block record (x at +0, y at +8, height at +10)
param load_stage_map_pointers R1 table_offset        # stage_floor_block_bounds[stage]: offset of the stage's list from 10E29C
param load_stage_map_pointers R10 bounds_list        # 10E29C + the offset, also stored to floor_block_bounds
param run_stage_events R1 table_offset               # stage_events[stage] (offset from 002492), set only on the stage's first call
param run_stage_events R10 event                     # stage_event_cursor: the (scroll position, game mode) record, + 2 once reached
param reset_trackball_step R3 player_number          # clears trackball_step_sums[R3]; run_game_mode passes 0; kept for read_trackball_step
param read_trackball_step R3 player_number           # in: the player (20F062 + 4n, 20F0B6 + 2n); out (low half): the step +1 / -1 / 0 that run_game_mode adds to stage
param read_trackball_step R10 trackball              # 20F062 + 4n: the player's trackball count it adds up
param update_restart_point R4 position               # mov.h 6435[R25], R4: scroll_position, compared with each 8-byte record
param start_player_objects_alt R3 player_number      # reset_objects_from_list's R3, handed back
param start_player_objects_alt R11 object            # passed to reset_objects_from_list
param start_player_objects R10 handler_cursor        # reset_objects_from_list's R10, handed back
param start_player_objects R11 object                # passed to reset_objects_from_list
param reset_objects_from_list R3 player_number       # 1 or 2 (from the player block at 20F0EE): player_status[R3]; else what reset_objects left
param reset_objects_from_list R10 handler_cursor     # walks the list at 20F0EA (count, then handlers), 4 bytes per handler; out = past the last one read
param reset_objects_from_list R11 object             # the object being started (allocate_object_or_start_list / allocate_object); the incoming value is only kept when no object is free
param check_hits R11 previous                        # the anchor before check_hit's first object: the hitter (its 68 = next) or 20F018 (its 68 = touchable_list)
param check_hit R10 other                            # walks the list it tests against (hit_list_next, 68)
param check_hit R11 previous                         # the object before R10 in that list (mov.h R10, R11 before advancing)
param check_hit R17 hitter                           # the object tested; both get flags bit 2 and touched_by on a hit
param check_platforms R8 load_count                  # the bridge load list's count after inc.b [R11], used as the index to append the platform's 6F
param check_platforms R10 platform                   # walks platform_list (platform_list_next, 72); out = the last one tested
param check_platforms R11 load_list                  # 209400 or 209500 (by the platform's 95): the bridge load list it appends to
param compute_bridge_sag R1 middle                   # R19 >> 1: plank numbers past it count from the far end (min(n, count - n))
param compute_bridge_sag R2 plank                    # the entry's plank number (movz.bw [R10+], R2)

# ======== scratch work RAM as each routine uses it (scoped global lines, from the helpers) ========
scoped global stage_clear_banner_hold 20F0EA banner_letter_offset_x u16  # x of the next letter from the banner's screen_x: 8, + 10 a letter (add.h into the letter's 0E)
scoped global stage_clear_banner_hold 20F0EC banner_letters_left s16  # the first halfword at the banner's animation (48): letters left (dec.h + bgt) and each letter's number (its kind, 47); its bit 0 (a test1 of the 32-bit word, left as temp_1) sets sprite flags bit 7 on odd letters
scoped global spawn_banner_sparkle 20F0EA sparkle_offset_x u16  # R0 (offset_x) kept across allocate_object: added to the banner's screen_x for the sparkle
scoped global start_player_objects 20F0EA player_handler_list u32  # player_objects (002405) or player_objects_alt (00241F): the list reset_objects_from_list starts objects from (its object_handler_list)
scoped global reset_objects_from_list 20F0EA object_handler_list u32  # set by start_player_objects(_alt): a count and that many handlers, read once into handler_cursor
scoped global reset_objects_from_list 20F0EE player_block_cursor u32  # 208400 (the first player block), + 200 a handler: its is_joining (9) set gives player_join, else player_status picks player_resume; 208600 = player 1, past it player 2
scoped global player_animate 20F0EA saved_sprite_offset_y u8  # sprite_offset_y kept while project_object runs with 12 (three places, 6 accesses); the climb pull-up (004D9B) keeps animate_around_anchor's last-step flag in the same byte (2 accesses), and the climbing side step its new screen_x as a long (004A77, 2 accesses: not named)
scoped global player_animate 20F0EE side_step_projected_y u32  # climbing side step: projected_y +- 1.0 (half the 2.0 x step, sign from the record byte), checked against the record's range and the screen, then copied into projected_y
scoped global compute_camera_slope_speed 20F0EA slope_velocity_y u32  # (camera_velocity_y << B) / (10000 + |slope_factor|): squared into camera_slope_speed, then the dy of angle_of_vector for camera_slope_direction
scoped global compute_scroll_drift 20F0EA unused_drift_divisor u32  # 10000 + |floor_slope_factors[slope]|, the divisor of camera_velocity_y << B: stored, never read back (compute_camera_slope_speed keeps its quotient there and does read it)
scoped global compute_scroll_drift 20F0EE unused_drift_byte u8  # the R9 byte both callers pass (0): stored, never read
scoped global check_player_step 20F0EA step_floor_z s32  # the floor height at the new position: floor_z, or the platform's z (flat platforms); z takes it for steps of 8 or less; compared signed with z after a blocked step
scoped global check_player_step 20F0EC step_floor_z_int u16  # its whole part (the high half): z_int minus it is the step
scoped global check_player_step 20F0EE step_blocking_floor_block u32  # floor_block of a step too high, kept while the previous block is restored: get_floor_block_side of it gives the bounce direction (speed_int >= 500, state E)
scoped global spawn_slip_pieces 20F0EA slip_pieces_left s16  # 2, counted down (dec.h + bgt)
scoped global spawn_slip_pieces 20F0EC slip_piece_speed u32  # 8000 (0.5 a frame), negated for the second piece: its speed_x (ledge sides 0/2/4) or speed_y (1/3)
scoped global spawn_player_ride 20F0EA ride_start_x u32  # A60 or AE0 (16.16), by the side the player is past: the ridden object's x
scoped global check_player_contacts 20E500 contact_saved_x u32  # kind 19 (pushes players along): x before the player is put back at previous_x for side_of_box; restored when the side is 8 (before it in x)
scoped global check_player_contacts 20E504 contact_saved_y u32  # the same for y
scoped global check_player_contacts 20F0EA contact_box_side u16  # side_of_box's R3 bits (8 before it in x, 4 past it, 2 before it in y, 1 past it; 0 none): 0 and 8 move the player with the object
scoped global spawn_ring_rows 20E500 ring_row_rings_left s16  # the record's count: rings left in the row (dec.h + bgt), one template object and one pool 2 shadow each
scoped global spawn_ring_rows 20E502 ring_row_template u16  # the record's offset into stage_object_templates (every ring of the row)
scoped global spawn_ring_rows 20E504 ring_row_x u16  # x of the next ring: the record's x, + ring_row_dx a ring
scoped global spawn_ring_rows 20E506 ring_row_y u16  # y of the next ring: the record's y, + ring_row_dy a ring
scoped global spawn_ring_rows 20E508 ring_row_dx u16  # the record's s8 dx (movs.bh)
scoped global spawn_ring_rows 20E50A ring_row_dy u16  # the record's s8 dy (movs.bh)
scoped global spawn_ring_rows 20E50C ring_row_next_80 u16  # 0, + 20 a ring: each ring's halfword 80 (ring_spin writes 78 there at each glint; no reader found)
scoped global scatter_rings 20F0EA scatter_fixed u16  # FFFF from scatter_rings_fixed, 0 from scatter_rings_random: low byte set = no random speed, high byte (scatter_fixed_jump) set = no random jump; scatter_rings then keeps each odd ring's random direction here (the next ring mirrors it: 400 - it), which overwrites both bytes for the rings after it. The low byte test (1 access, AS8) is not named
scoped global scatter_rings 20F0EB scatter_fixed_jump u8  # high byte of scatter_fixed: 0 = upward speed_z from next_random (& 1FFFF + 80000), else speed_z stays 0

# A formatted text: a position word (text map offset, 31F000 | word), an attribute byte, then runs of characters ending
# in 0, each followed by a code byte that jumps through a table of 3-byte branches right after the run's loop (0996A7,
# 099703, 099764 to print; 0997BC, 0997FD, 099841 to erase): 0 end; 3/6/9 next run at 1/2/3 cells per character;
# C new attribute byte, same width; F/15/1B new position word and attribute byte at width 1/2/3; 12/18/1E new
# attribute byte at width 1/2/3; 21 skip s8 cells, 24 skip s16 cells (same width). Width 2 writes cell, cell + 1;
# width 3 cell, cell + 1, cell + 2 (a character drawn as 2 or 3 consecutive tiles). The eraser walks the same
# records writing R0 (0) and skipping the attribute bytes; its tables have no entry 24 (it would land inside 21's code).

# The flood fill queue records (0x1A bytes) as flood_fill_push_span writes them through R23 (object_cursor)
struct flood_fill_record 1A                     # one span the unused flood_fill queues (ring of them at 20B500-20CCC3, written through R23, read through R24)

field flood_fill_record 02 right_x u16  # flood_fill_span's R16
field flood_fill_record 04 right_address u32  # flood_fill_span's R15

field flood_fill_record 0A left_address u32  # flood_fill_span's R14
field flood_fill_record 0E parent_right_x u16  # flood_fill_push_parent_right_x
field flood_fill_record 10 parent_right_address u32  # flood_fill_push_parent_right_address
field flood_fill_record 14 parent_left_x u16  # flood_fill_push_parent_left_x
field flood_fill_record 16 parent_left_address u32  # flood_fill_push_parent_left_address

struct chase_step_with_limit C rom               # an entry of a chaser's path (tools/formats/stages.py _chase_path_recs, keys "at" then a coordinate): fire_front, rising_saw, lava_flow and the leading burning_boulder keep the next one in their field 80 (path) and step it with [R10+] (fire_front_read_script 08B038/08B045 then fire_front_load_record 08B0A2-08B0B4; rising_saw_read_script 08B5C5-08B5F5; lava_flow_read_script 087641-08767E; burning_boulder_update 0864E9-086510), path = the next one (+ C); an 8-byte "stop" (no base_speed, wait_timer) ends a path; census ROM 08BDAD-08BDF0 and 08BDF9-08BE24 (fire_front_paths), 08C00D-08C044, 08C04B-08C082 and 08C089-08C0CC (rising_saw_paths), 087B7F-087BAA (burning_boulder_speed_script), 087D21-087D40 (lava_flow_script); the geyser front (geyser_front_read_script 08C83A-08C84D) and the propeller machine (propeller_machine_read_script 08D44E-08D463) read the same entries

# ======== what the C says above each function (build/naming/comments_1..8.txt) ========
comment add_to_hitter_list Puts current_object at the head of hitter_list (linked by hit_list_next) and clears its flags bits 2 (hit) and 27 (in a zone) for this frame's check_hits and check_zones.
comment add_to_platform_list Puts current_object at the head of platform_list (linked by platform_list_next) and clears its flags bit 3, which check_platforms sets when a rider stands on it.
comment add_to_rider_list Puts current_object at the head of rider_list (linked by platform_list_next) and clears its flags bits 3 (on a platform) and 5 (in a wall) for check_platforms and check_walls.
comment add_to_touchable_list Puts current_object at the head of touchable_list (linked by hit_list_next), which check_hits tests the hitters against, and clears its flags bits 2 (hit) and 6 (hit by a player's attack).
comment add_to_wall_list Puts current_object, a wall, at the head of wall_list (linked by platform_list_next) and clears its flags bit 5, which check_walls sets when a rider is inside it.
comment add_to_zone_list Puts current_object at the head of zone_list (linked by hit_list_next) and clears its flags bit 27, which check_zones sets when a hitter is inside its box.
comment check_hit Tests hitter against the list from other on, skipping pairs whose kinds are both 2 or less: circle against circle (skewed on a slope), point against box, box against round or box against box (flags bit 1: a box) in x and y, then the heights. The first hit sets flags bit 2, touch_distance and touched_by (the other) in both.
comment check_hits Tests each object of hitter_list against the hitters after it (check_hit) and then, unless that has already hit it (flags bit 2; the last hitter is always tested), against touchable_list. Empties both lists for the next frame.
comment check_platforms Matches each rider with the first platform whose box (no offsets) holds its x and y: rider flags bit 3, platform pointing at each other. A rider not above floor_z sets the platform's bit 3, the first adding its member_number to a bridge load list (by spawn_arg_2_high). Then compute_bridge_sag per bridge; both lists emptied.
comment check_walls Matches each rider of rider_list with the first wall of wall_list whose box holds its x and y and whose height (hitbox_height up from its z) holds the rider's z: flags bit 5 on both and wall pointing at each other. Empties wall_list.
comment check_zones Matches each hitter of hitter_list with the first object of zone_list whose box holds its x and y and whose height overlaps its own: flags bit 27 on both and anchor_x pointing at each other. Empties zone_list (check_hits empties hitter_list).
comment compute_bridge_sag Fills a bridge's sag table, which check_platforms passes in current_player, from load_list: with only the ends 0 and plank_count (no plank loaded) it is cleared; else the loaded planks are sorted and the table gets straight lines between consecutive ones, each sagging bridge_sag_curve[distance to the nearer end] << 8.
comment biting_head_catch_up_speed Moves the biting head (biting_head_move_at_speed) at the camera's speed on its slope (compute_camera_slope_speed with its floor_slope_factors entry) times catch_up_factor / 0x100, or at base_speed when that is higher.
comment biting_head_chase Each frame of the biting head's chase: biting_head_read_script, or biting_head_chase_step while it holds back. From its second frame, when no_player_in_play, player_mishap or player_dropping_in is set, it starts holding back: base_speed 0 and screen_threshold 0x160 (-0x20 in directions 1 and 2), the old ones saved.
comment biting_head_chase_step Projects the biting head, puts its second box 0x40 further in x (same y and z) and both boxes in the zone list. A hold-back ends, restoring screen_threshold and base_speed, after 0x300 of scroll or when hold_timer runs out (it only counts in game_mode 3), going to biting_head_catch_up_speed; otherwise biting_head_choose_speed.
comment biting_head_choose_speed Moves the biting head at base_speed while it is within screen_threshold (screen_x at most it in directions 0 and 3, at least it in 1, 2 and 4); beyond it, or above the screen (screen_y below 0), it drops its wait and any hold-back and catches up (biting_head_catch_up_speed).
comment biting_head_init Sets up the biting head: x, y and path from biting_head_paths (by its sprite_frame), kind 9 (hurts) with a 0x80 x 0x40 box 0xF0 high, a part block from take_free_object (biting_head_parts and two clip entries) and a second 0x200 x 0x130 box as its child; biting_head = it, biting_head_done = 0; then biting_head_wait.
comment biting_head_load_record Loads the biting head's next path record from path_cursor: screen_threshold, catch_up_factor, base_speed, wait_timer and direction, path moving past it. A negative factor ends the chase: the part block (sprite_frame here is the low half of part_list) and the second box are freed and the head deleted.
comment biting_head_move_at_speed Sets chaser_speed = move_speed; after the wait the head moves that much along its direction. Moving, parts 0 and 4 cycle biting_head_move_frames and it bobs; the jaw (part 3) bites, step 5 shaking it (biting_head_bounce). Boxes 0x50 high from x -0x355, biting_head_done from -0x431; drawn (with its clip entries before scroll 0x1500).
comment biting_head_read_script Counts the biting head's wait_timer down; once it is out, loads the next path record (biting_head_load_record) when scroll_position reaches its scroll word or the head reaches its coordinate along its direction (y in 0, 2 and 4, x in 1 and 3); then biting_head_chase_step.
comment biting_head_wait Keeps the biting head waiting until chaser_stopped is set, or sets it itself once scroll_position reaches 0x1200; then biting_head_chase.
comment brick_dust_animate A dust puff of the bursting brick wall: hidden while its wait_timer runs, then plays brick_dust_animation once and is deleted.
comment brick_wall_init Sets up the brick wall: frame 0x7D90, palette 0x10D0, standing at z 0x1D8 (its floor_z too), projected; brick_wall_wait runs it.
comment brick_wall_wait Draws the brick wall until chaser_stopped is set, then bursts it: brick_wall_bricks bricks from brick_wall_brick_records (screen offsets, speeds, animations) fly off as rock_debris_fly, brick_wall_dust dust puffs start from brick_wall_dust_records (brick_dust_animate), and the wall is deleted.
comment build_grate_steps Builds the grating steps, one row a frame once 6 objects are free: three steps (frame 0x7FF0, grate_step_update) 0x35 apart in projected x, each with its column 0-2 in kind and cut_z 0x1E below it; each row 0x1E lower down the floor's slope. Deletes itself after 15 rows.

comment falling_grate_update A grate in a row led by its parent (current_player is borrowed for the leader): a platform, drawn at screen_y + depth_offset; within 0x60 of the leader it rattles (z up and down 1), and when the leader reaches it in y or x by its direction it plays sound 0xD and falls (falling_grate_animation), a platform at first, until off the bottom.
comment fire_front_chase Each frame of the fire front's chase, as biting_head_chase: fire_front_read_script, or fire_front_chase_step while it holds back (base_speed and speeds 0). Its hold screen_threshold is direction ^ (direction >> 1), 0x160 only in direction 0, not the biting head's -0x20 or 0x160.

comment fire_front_load_record Loads the fire front's next path record from path_cursor: screen_threshold, catch_up_factor, base_speed and wait_timer (a wait stops its speeds), path moving past it. A negative factor ends the chase: chaser_object = 0 and the front is deleted.
comment fire_front_read_script As biting_head_read_script for the fire front: once wait_timer is out, the next record loads when scroll_position reaches its scroll word or the front reaches its coordinate (y + hitbox_offset_y in directions 0 and 4); a coordinate of 0 waits for the scroll only.
comment grate_step_debris_fly A piece of grate step debris: falls (gravity 0x6000), moves speed_x in projected x, animates at depth 0xE0 and is deleted off screen.

comment add_push_to_player_motion Unused: polar_to_xy(heading_snapped, speed_int) plus the push, each >> 4, gives speed (length << 12, 0 when negative, at most 0x5000000) and heading; the push is then cleared. comment check_fall_into_pit Over a pit (floor_z 0x7FF or more, not floor type 6), a player falling or still (speed_z not negative) at or below its previous floor's height goes to state 9, falling into the pit.
comment check_player_contacts What touching an object does to the player, by the kind of the object in touched_by: rings (3 and 42) give rings and health, hazards hurt (state 0xD) or tumble it, solid kinds stop or bounce it, others launch, hold, catch or sink it. Nothing on a path (but 0x14-0x16), untouched, or when the object has flags bit 9.
comment check_player_contacts_attack A jumping player hits toucher once (last_damaged): toucher gets flags bit 6 and loses attack_power health. If that finishes it and it is not a sturdy kind (9, 0xB-0xE, 0x11, 0x18, 0x19), the player gets hit_stop 3; else it is thrown back with a hop, along toucher's direction (flags bit 30) or back the way it came.
comment check_player_contacts_attack_or_hurt A jumping player attacks toucher (check_player_contacts_attack); otherwise it is hurt (state 0xD), taking new_substate and hurt_contact_delay 2 only for a new toucher (last_hazard).
comment check_player_contacts_clear_state Nothing holds the player: pushed_out 0, last_hazard and last_damaged 0xFFFF (the next touch counts as new), flags bits 18, 23 and 31 off and block flags bit 1 off.
comment check_player_contacts_hurt Hurts the player with substate 0 (check_player_contacts_attack_or_hurt), so a jumping player attacks instead.
comment check_player_contacts_hurt_unless_invulnerable Ignores toucher while invulnerable_timer runs (check_player_contacts_clear_state); else check_player_contacts_hurt.
comment check_player_contacts_solid The player against a solid object: jumping, it attacks it; otherwise it goes back to its previous place and floor and bounces (state 0xE) at speed 0x500 or more (not off kind 0x20) or stops. After 0x1E frames on the same object it is pushed out toward the screen centre (pushed_out); climbing, it undoes the climb step.
comment check_player_floor_edge Jumping with no floor block under it, the player goes over the edge (state 7, substate 1, ledge_side and fall_draw_depth set); on the ground over a pit (floor_z past 0x7FF) it teeters (5), or goes over (7) faster than 0x200 off most block types or with block flags bit 1. Stage 0: 0x18 at once; 4: when goal_unlocked; 5: 0x18 with scene_path 0xB, or 0x11 once the spiked press has stood 0x258 frames.
comment check_player_step Sets step_floor_z, the height the player stands on: its floor_z, or a flat platform's z (snapped to at once over a block of type 0x24); then check_player_step_against_floor. In stage 8 before scroll 0x4000 the player just snaps to its floor.
comment check_player_step_against_floor Puts the player on step_floor_z: on a path or within 8, z snaps to it (previous_z keeps the old z); a lower floor starts a fall (state 2); a higher one blocks it unless sloped: back to its previous place and floor, bouncing (state 0xE, away from the block's side) at speed 0x500 or more, else stopping (state 0).
comment check_scene_states Forces the states of the current game mode and events on a playing player: 0x19 (mode 0xD), 0x1E (1), 0x2B (0x18), 0x30 (0x19, bridge collapsing), 0x31 (0x1A), the ride of mode 0x1C (spawn_player_ride, then 0x35), 0x21 (0x17, 0x1D, 4), 0x26 (players_pulled), 0x38 (mode 3 in stage 0xB, y up to 0x500), 0x39 (0x20).

comment compute_ground_speed Sets ground_speed = (speed >> 8) x heading_speed_factors[(heading + 0x20) >> 6]; on a slope it is scaled by the slope_speed_direction_pairs entry for floor_slope and direction, whose second word becomes direction.

comment follow_player_path The player's autopilot: takes a new path from path_request or all_players_path_request (follow_player_path_start) or runs the current one (follow_player_path_run), and hands back the speed to aim for: the path's, or target_speed with no path.
comment follow_player_path_aim_at_point Turns target_heading and facing_angle toward the point of the current path record (its x and y words) and, on a path's first record (flags bit 0, cleared here), heading too; then follow_player_path_target_speed.
comment follow_player_path_load_record Starts the path record at path_pointer: path_speed from it; its flag bit 0 makes the player jump (state 4); a speed of 0 makes it wait path_wait (the record's second word) frames, else it heads for the record's point (follow_player_path_aim_at_point).

comment follow_player_path_run Runs the current path: during a wait the speed to aim for is 0 (speed stopped below 0x20) until path_wait runs out; else the player heads for the record's point until within 8 in x and y (at once with the record's flag bit 1), then the next record.
comment follow_player_path_start Starts path on the player: path_pointer from player_path_offsets[path + player], speed 0, z on its floor, state 1, flags bits 6 and 13 off and bit 0 on (so the first aim sets heading too); then its first record.
comment follow_player_path_target_speed Hands back path_speed << 16 as the speed to aim for; a slow path (0x20 or less) gives 0, and stops the player, once its speed is under 0x20.
comment get_floor_block_side Hands back which side of floor block floor_block the point x, y is on: 3 before x_min, 1 past x_max, else 0 before y_min and 2 otherwise (y_max is not checked: the point is taken to be outside the block).
comment get_floor_block_side_or_corner Unused: as get_floor_block_side with the corners: hands back the outcode of x, y against block (1 past x_max, 2 before x_min, 4 before y_min, 8 past y_max) and side_code = floor_block_side_codes[outcode].

comment pay_and_join Joins the player when it has cost credits (none on free play) and its start button (trackball button with setting_no_start_buttons) is newly pressed, from the shared or its own credit block by cabinet_config: credits taken, cabinet event written, io_port_d bit cleared on 2-player setups, credits saved, -1 handed back; else joined.

comment player_dispatch_state Runs the code of the player's state: player_move for the moving states (0, 1, 2, 4, 12, 19, 20, 23 and 58), one player_state_ function for each other state. State code that changes the state calls it again, so the new state runs in the same frame.
comment player_join The handler of a player who paid to join: player_status 4 and the character select (player_select_character) until it is done, except when current_game_mode and game_mode are both 0x1B; then player_reset_joined.
comment player_place Places the player at its restart point on its floor (start_climb_at_spawn on a wall) and sets entry_status and player_status: 0x81 over a pit or while touched or in a zone, 0x82 waiting for the scene (set_player_entry_by_scene), else 0xFF, staying the handler while it waits; then add_player_to_lists and player_hud_start.
comment player_reset Resets the player for a start or a respawn: speeds, movement, path and timers cleared, state 0, 0x78 frames invulnerable and blinking unless a stage starts (flags bit 25), the stage's palette for its character; plays its character's join or respawn voice unless a stage starts or current_game_mode is 0x1B; then player_place.
comment player_reset_joined After joining: block flags bit 4, health = starting_health, rings_to_health 0 and, unless a stage exit is under way, unused_player_flags and players_finished cleared for it; then player_reset.
comment player_respawn The handler set for a player that comes back after losing health (off screen, sunk, fallen): player_restart without the stage-start flag (flags bit 25).
comment player_restart Restarts the player: in a game (in_game above 0) player_reset; otherwise it does not play: in_game 0, state 0xB (0x37 for the third player on a 2-player cabinet), player_update as its handler.
comment player_resume Makes player_update the handler, for a player already in the stage (reset_objects_from_list sets it).
comment player_start A new game for the player object: links it with its player block (current_player), health = starting_health, rings 0, kind = player (its character), state 0xB (0x37 for the third player on a 2-player cabinet), two full-screen clip entries; in_game 1 when try_join succeeds. Next comes player_start_stage.
comment player_start_stage The player's handler at a stage start: flags bit 25 (a stage start), block flags bit 4 off, stage_rings 0, the HUD records (player_hud_init), then player_restart.
comment player_steer Steers the player on the ground: a path gives the speed (player_steer_approach_speed); else the trackball (zeroed while players_frozen) or a push turns target_heading (not with flags bit 13) and sets the speed (player_steer_speed_from_trackball); with no input it slows down and, under speed 0x20, stops and stands (state 0).
comment player_steer_approach_speed Brings speed toward wanted_speed (apply_speed_scale): up at once and down 1/32 of the gap (up 1/32, down 1/64 on floor type 7), sets animation_speed, and picks standing (0), walking (1), running (0x13) or fast running (0x14) by it, except in states 4, 0x17, 0x25, 0x26 and 0x2D; then player_steer_turn_and_ground_speed.
comment player_steer_in_air Steers the player in the air: speed goes to the trackball's (its length squared, at most 0x5000000) at once when higher, by 1/32 of the gap when lower; the trackball turns target_heading unless flags bit 13 is set; then turn_player.
comment player_steer_speed_from_trackball The wanted speed is 1.5 x the length of trackball + push squared, at most 0x5000000; a quarter of it with flags bit 31 (0 with block flags bit 2), slowed by sink_depth on floor type 0xA (setting struggle_speed), 0x60/0x100 of it on floor type 4; then player_steer_approach_speed.
comment player_steer_turn_and_ground_speed Runs turn_player, then sets ground_speed: speed scaled by heading_speed_factors for the heading (speed itself with flags bit 31), and on a slope by the slope_speed_direction_pairs entry, which also sets direction (as compute_ground_speed).

comment push_player_from_screen_edge Pushes the player 0x200 along the angle screen_edge_push_directions gives for screen_edge; when its direction is not within a quarter turn after that entry's direction, it first goes back to its previous position, floor block and floor_z.
comment push_player_out_of_wall In a wall's box (flags bit 5, wall) the player goes back to its previous place and floor, for 0x1E frames per wall. comment set_climb_speed_from_trackball As set_speed_from_trackball for climbing: speed at most 0x3000000 and direction the trackball's angle itself.

comment set_fall_sprite_priority Sets the player's sprite priority bits for its fall into a pit from fall_sprite_priorities: the entry of the block it fell from, by ledge_side (ledge_direction when 4), or by the half of the block it is over when the block it left is of type 0x11 or 0x1F, or its current one 0x1D or 0x1E; a negative entry leaves them.

comment draw_line_shallow_even_pixel Part of draw_line at 4 bpp, more columns than rows: puts color in the low nibble (an even x) of the pixel's byte; if the line stays on the row it goes on to the odd pixel of the same byte (draw_line_shallow_set_high_nibble), else it writes the byte and steps a row (draw_line_shallow_odd_pixel).

At 4 bpp the rows of 4-pixel blocks go up from the bottom, each starting a row above where the last ended: they slant, and a full-width fill rewrites only the bottom row.
comment fill_span_4bpp The horizontal line of draw_line at 4 bits per pixel, from start_x to end_x on row start_y (two pixels a byte, the even one in the low nibble): a lone odd first pixel, a whole byte at an odd address, then 8 pixels a long store and a masked long for the rest.
comment fill_span_8bpp Fills length + 1 bytes of the 8 bpp bitmap with color from pixel_address: an odd first byte, blocks of 16 in long stores, then 8, 4, 2 and 1; hands back pixel_address at the last byte written. Used for draw_line's horizontal lines and the rectangles' rows.

comment debris_fly A debris piece: move_object_projected, removed off screen (delete_if_off_screen), fall_to_floor.
