comment compute_camera_ground_speed When camera_velocity_x/_y changed (camera_ground_speed_vx/_vy): camera_ground_speed = sqrt(vx * vx + vy * vy) << 13 with vx, vy the velocities >> 5 and >> 4, camera_ground_direction the angle of (>> 9, >> 8) + 0x80, camera_map_direction the angle of (>> 8, >> 8); hands back that angle's octant (else octant as it came).
comment compute_camera_slope_speed The same on a floor slope (slope_factor, 0 flat), recomputed only when the velocity or slope_factor changed: camera_slope_speed, camera_slope_direction (+ 0x80), camera_scroll_direction (angle of the velocities >> 5). On a slope camera_velocity_y is taken >> 5 and divided by 1 + |slope_factor| (16.16), not >> 4 as when flat.
comment debug_sprite_mover_update Unused: the debug sprite's handler: sprite 0x8DB8 (palette 0x130, layer 0x32) at debug_sprite_x, debug_sprite_y; held 1P jump and 1P start move it right and left, 2P jump and input bit 25 down and up, a pixel a frame; the two are shown in hex at text cells (3,22) and (8,22).
comment get_tile_set_list Hands back in script_list the vram script list of tile set tile_set from the stage's table at script_list: 16-bit offsets from blank_tile_set_lists for stages 0-2 and 0x11-0x13, 32-bit pointers for the others; stage_offset gets stage * 2.
comment get_tile_set_list_bank Hands back script_list + 0x100000 for stages 3-0x10 and 0x13, unchanged for stages 0-2, 0x11 and 0x12.
comment get_tile_set_script_bank Hands back script + 0x100000 for stages 3-0x10 and 0x13, unchanged for stages 0-2, 0x11 and 0x12.
comment index_stage_list_pair Unused: reads two per-stage tables at once: first_entry and second_entry each become the long at their address + stage_offset, plus section_offset.
comment init_stage_view Sets up a stage's view: display off 8 frames, default palettes, the tile sets of stage_initial_tile_sets, zoom, blending, the NBG1-3 layers; the camera at the stage's origin, view offsets, scroll_end and the first section's speeds, limits, scroll mode and direction from the per-stage tables; scene steps, shake and scroll skip panel reset.
comment is_direction_in_quadrant Looks through count entries of sine_table from sine_entry for the pair section_direction_y lies between: found (1 in its low byte) with sine_entry left there, or 0 after count entries; a direction straight along an axis (0x4000 or 0xC000, the other 0) is found at once.
comment is_player_at_bottom_edge Hands back 1 (at_edge's low byte) when object's screen_y is at or below push_edge_bottom, else 0; 0xA past it also sets player_past_leading_edge.
comment is_player_at_diagonal_edge_30 Hands back 1 (at_edge's low byte) when object is on or above the line screen_y = screen_x / 2 + edge_offset; a second pass at edge_offset - 0xA sets player_past_leading_edge, which it clears first. Its inner test, screen_x against 2 * (screen_y - edge_offset), is the same line and never passes.
comment is_player_at_diagonal_edge_60 Hands back 1 (at_edge's low byte) when object is on or below the line screen_y = screen_x / 2 + edge_offset. It clears player_past_leading_edge, and its second pass, at edge_offset - 0xA, takes the line 0xA back, so both count from 0xA before the line; its inner test is the same line and never passes.
comment is_player_at_diagonal_edge_c0 Hands back 1 (at_edge's low byte) when object is on or above the line screen_y = edge_offset - screen_x / 2; a second pass at edge_offset - 0xA sets player_past_leading_edge, which it clears first. Its inner test is the same line and never passes.
comment is_player_at_diagonal_edge_f0 Hands back 1 (at_edge's low byte) when object is on or below the line screen_y = edge_offset - screen_x / 2. It clears player_past_leading_edge, and its second pass, at edge_offset - 0xA, takes the line 0xA back, so both count from 0xA before the line; its inner test is the same line and never passes.
comment is_player_at_left_edge Hands back 1 (at_edge's low byte) when object's screen_x is at or left of push_edge_left, else 0; 0xA past it also sets player_past_leading_edge.
comment is_player_at_right_edge Hands back 1 (at_edge's low byte) when object's screen_x is at or right of push_edge_right, else 0; 0xA past it also sets player_past_leading_edge.
comment is_player_at_top_edge Hands back 1 (at_edge's low byte) when object's screen_y is at or above push_edge_top, else 0; 0xA past it also sets player_past_leading_edge.
comment is_player_facing_scroll Hands back 1 (facing's low byte) when heading, a target_heading, is within a quarter turn either side of the middle of the scroll's quadrant (sine_entry's quarter of sine_table: 0x180, 0x280, 0x380 or 0x80), else 0.
comment is_player_pushing_edge Hands back 1 (pushing's low byte) when the player object object is at a leading screen edge for push_edge_case (the push_edge_* lines and, in cases 2, 4, 6 and 8, a diagonal); at a trailing edge it sets player_at_trailing_edge and hands back 0. In stage 3 between scroll_position 0x87A9 and 0x96F1 case 8 counts only the top edge.
comment load_camera_start_section Puts the camera and the scroll at the start of section stage_start_section of the stage's tables, as init_stage_view does for the first: camera_x/_y at the section's start (+ camera_origin_x/_y), its x and y limits and direction, scroll_position at its start and its end next, scroll_speed, follow_base_speed and its scroll mode.
comment load_tile_set Loads tile set tile_set of the stage: every vram script of its list in stage_tile_sets (up to a negative entry) through run_vram_script, list and scripts moved for the stage (get_tile_set_list_bank, _script_bank); then tile_sets_in_progress = wanted_tile_sets, which loaded_tile_sets takes after the fourth slot (tile_set_slot 0 again).
comment move_camera_along_path Moves the camera along the section by speed: camera_x/_y by section_direction_x/_y * speed unless that passes section_limit_x/_y (from camera_origin, the way the limits run), scroll_position unless it passes the section end; camera_limits_reached keeps which stopped (all three: snap_camera_to_section_end). Hands back scroll_position + speed.
comment move_camera_to_start_section load_camera_start_section, then update_camera_view; y gets view_y.
comment reload_changed_tile_set Checks one slot of wanted_tile_sets a frame (tile_set_slot, from 0 again when the wanted sets changed): a set not among the four of loaded_tile_sets is loaded (load_tile_set). Meanwhile tile_sets_in_progress keeps the wanted sets; after the fourth slot loaded_tile_sets takes them and tile_set_slot is 0 again.
comment run_scroll_skip_mode Unused: the scroll skip panel's frame. Closed (scroll_skip_open 0), it opens while service and 2P start are held (input_ports_active bits 0 and 5): scroll_skip_last_point for the stage, stage_start_section 0xD, armed flags cleared, the panel printed. Open: scroll_skip_draw_values, _next_point, _previous_point, _check_call, _check_exit.
comment run_stage_05_switch Stage 5's switch to stage 0's view by stage_05_switch_step: every layer blended, a fade to black, stage 0's tile layers (coast, horizon, sky, city, tower top) with the camera at 0xF80,0x670 and NBG1-3 scrolled as stage 0's, a fade in from black; then scroll_position 0x5E5A, stage 0, blending off and stage_05_switch_step -1.
comment scroll_at_scroll_speed Scroll mode 0: advance_scroll_unless_ended at scroll_speed.
comment scroll_skip_check_call Unused: "CALL:1P START": 1P start pressed after a release (scroll_skip_call_armed) moves the camera to stage_start_section (move_camera_to_start_section), every frame while it stays held, as the flag is not cleared; nothing while both starts are held.
comment scroll_skip_check_exit Unused: "EXIT:2P START": 2P start pressed after a release (scroll_skip_exit_armed) closes the panel (scroll_skip_open 0, scroll_skip_erase_panel); nothing while both starts are held.
comment scroll_skip_draw_values Unused: one value a frame (scroll_skip_value_index 0-2): the stage's entry for stage_start_section in scroll_skip_value_lists[index] (x position, y position, scroll total) in hex at its cell (attribute 0x200); after the third, stage_start_section in hex at (24,15) (attribute 0x600).
comment scroll_skip_erase_panel Unused: prints scroll_skip_blank_text over the panel (print_text_list).
comment scroll_skip_next_point Unused: "NEXT:1P JUMP": 1P jump pressed after a release (scroll_skip_next_armed) adds 1 to stage_start_section, which is kept at most scroll_skip_last_point; nothing while both jumps are held.
comment scroll_skip_previous_point Unused: "BACK:2P JUMP": 2P jump pressed after a release (scroll_skip_back_armed) takes 1 off stage_start_section, not below 0; nothing while both jumps are held.
comment scroll_skip_print_panel Unused: prints the scroll skip panel (scroll_skip_panel_text) with print_text_list.
comment scroll_skip_total_cell Unused: hands back text cell (34,17), where the SCROLL TOTAL value goes.
comment scroll_skip_x_position_cell Unused: hands back text cell (34,18), where the X POSITION value goes.
comment scroll_skip_y_position_cell Unused: hands back text cell (34,19), where the Y POSITION value goes.
comment scroll_slowing_down Scroll mode 3: scroll_speed - 1 each time scroll_mode_timer runs out (reloaded from scroll_mode_duration), down to 1; advances at scroll_speed (scroll_at_scroll_speed).
comment scroll_speeding_up Scroll mode 4: advances at scroll_ramp_speed, + 1 each time scroll_mode_timer runs out (reloaded from scroll_mode_duration); once it has reached scroll_speed, scroll mode 0 and scroll_ramp_speed 1, and that frame only set_camera_velocity with the speed its caller passed.
comment set_camera_velocity camera_velocity_x/_y = section_direction_x/_y * speed's low half; camera_shake_length and camera_shake_wave 0x200, update_camera_with_shake, then (unless scroll_ended) update_background_scroll.
comment set_nbg0_scroll_from_camera NBG0's scroll from the camera's pixels (x & 0x3FF, y & 0x1FF) and the camera's place in the stage's block map: tile_block_column = camera_x_pixels / 0x200, tile_block_row = camera_y_pixels / 0x100 * stage_block_map_width. Hands back scroll_x with camera_x_pixels in its low half.
comment set_screen_push_edges From section_direction_x/_y's signs: the quadrant (sine_entry at its quarter of sine_table, count 0x100 for is_direction_in_quadrant) and the screen edges players push in it (push_edge_left, _right, _top, _bottom; 0xFFFF none), with push_edge_case 1, 2, 4, 6, 7 or 8 (1 and 7 for straight +x and -y).
comment snap_camera_to_section_end Puts the camera at the section's x and y limits (+ camera_origin_x/_y) and scroll_position at the section's end.
comment spawn_debug_sprite_mover Unused: once per stage view (debug_sprite_spawned), an object with handler debug_sprite_mover_update (allocate_object_outside_loop).
comment start_stage_view init_stage_view for every stage but 0x11 (unused_scroll_flag set first, which init_stage_view clears); stage 0x11 only clears ending_scene_step.
comment update_background_scroll update_nbg1_scroll, update_nbg3_scroll and update_nbg2_scroll; then follow_base_speed is forced to 0x10 once scroll_position reaches the first position of the stage's stage_fast_scroll_ranges list past the current section's start.
comment update_camera_view camera_x_pixels and camera_y_pixels from camera_x/_y's whole parts, view_x/_y from them minus view_offset_x/_y; hands back view_y.
comment update_camera_view_y camera_y_pixels from y's whole part (16.16) and view_y = it minus view_offset_y, which it hands back.
comment update_camera_with_shake update_camera_view, then while camera_shake_active every other frame camera y moves by sine_table at camera_shake_wave + camera_shake_step (* 0x20: up to 8 pixels), the step going up 0xA a frame until camera_shake_length ends the shake; NBG0's scroll follows. Hands back view_y.
comment update_fade One step of a fade of the mixer's colour offsets (color_offset_red, _blue, _green) by fade_kind: 0 to black (0x3F down to 0x20), 1 from white (0x1F down to 0), 2 from black (0x20 up to 0x3F), 3 to white (0 up to 0x1F), fade_speed a frame; fade_step 0 sets the start, and fade_kind is -1 the frame after the end.
comment update_scroll The scroll's frame by scroll_mode (update_scroll_at_end from scroll_end on): 0 at scroll_speed, 1 stopped, 2 paused, then the next mode of scroll_mode_script, 3 slowing, 4 speeding up, 5/6 nearby_floor_blocks_locked set/cleared; 7 and 8 follow_base_speed plus the speed of the fastest player pushing a leading screen edge facing the scroll.
comment update_scroll_at_end scroll_ended = -1; only stage 3 goes on, its end by stage_03_end_step: two end scripts and NBG0's pages, the camera climbing straight up, sped up to run at 0x25 for stage_03_end_timer (0x78) frames; then camera_y 1, a third script, a slowdown to a stop, all_players_path_request 0x23 and spawn_stage_03_end_pillar; the camera then stays still.
comment update_stage_00_exit_scene Stage 0's exit by stage_00_exit_step: the camera climbs straight up at scroll_speed (0x35, later down to 2), the tower wall and beam scripts run as NBG0's y scroll passes 0x20 and 0xF6, pages changing with stage_00_exit_timer; a fade to white; then NBG0 and NBG1 zoom in on new pages (0x2000000 / stage_00_exit_zoom >> 8) as colours come back.
comment update_stage_tile_layers A stage frame's tile layers: animate_stage_palette, then (until scroll_ended) clamp_camera_pixels, NBG0's scroll and wanted_tile_sets from the 2 x 2 blocks of stage_block_maps around the camera, a set a byte; when they differ from loaded_tile_sets reload_changed_tile_set (a reload past its second slot keeps its sets), else tile_set_slot 0.
comment clip_line_at_x Moves the line's start dx along x: start_x += dx and start_y += (end_y - start_y) * dx / (end_x - start_x), start_y kept when the line is vertical; unclipped_y gets start_y before the move.
comment clip_line_at_y Moves the line's start dy along y: start_y += dy and start_x += (end_x - start_x) * dy / (end_y - start_y), start_x kept when the line is level; unclipped_y gets start_y before the move.
comment clip_line_end_inside Nothing to move: the end is inside bitmap_window (outcode 0), or its outcode has both left and right (3, 7, 11).
comment clip_line_to_bottom_edge Moves the line's start onto bitmap_window_bottom (clip_line_at_y by bitmap_window_bottom - start_y).
comment clip_line_to_left_edge Moves the line's start onto bitmap_window_left (clip_line_at_x by bitmap_window_left - start_x).
comment clip_line_to_right_edge Moves the line's start onto bitmap_window_right (clip_line_at_x by bitmap_window_right - start_x).
comment clip_line_to_top_edge Moves the line's start onto bitmap_window_top (clip_line_at_y by bitmap_window_top - start_y).
comment clip_line_to_window Clips a line to bitmap_window: moves its start onto the edge outcode names (top or bottom when a corner code also has left or right), then swaps the ends and does the same with end_outcode, so the line comes back with its ends swapped; unclipped_y gets the last moved end's y from before the move.
comment clip_rect_to_window Sorts the rectangle left, top, right, bottom and clips it to bitmap_window: unclipped_edges comes back 0 when it lies wholly outside, else 0xF less a bit for each edge moved (1 left, 2 right, 4 top, 8 bottom). The outside tests take left and top unsigned, so a rectangle starting at a negative x or y counts as outside.
comment draw_circle Unused: a midpoint circle of radius |radius| around x, y in color, eight points a step (plot_circle_point_8bpp or _4bpp), none when it is wholly outside bitmap_window. current_player holds 2 bits a point (plot, or plot if inside), but points 4, 6 and 7 are plotted out of the order they assume; at 4 bpp odd pixels get color << 3, not << 4.
comment draw_circle_polygon Unused: meant to draw a circle of radius |radius| around center_x, center_y in circle_color: 64 points (sine_table * radius >> 14 mirrored into eight octants) in bitmap_draw_buffer joined by draw_line. It cannot: two mirrored stores are off (mirror_cursor + 0x7E, point_cursor + 0x7F) and the line loop steps 2 bytes, joining (x, y) to (y, next x).
comment draw_saved_bitmap_rect Unused: meant to copy a save_bitmap_rect buffer back onto the bitmap row by row, from its saved_bitmap_rect header (row_bits, rows); the row copy is an instruction the V60 cannot run, so the C stops at invalid_operand on the first row.
comment fill_flat_top_triangle Unused: the triangle with its top edge from left_x to right_x on row top_y and its apex at bottom_x, height rows lower: both edges stepped in 16.16, one polygon_span a row at span_cursor (addresses from current_player, 0x200 a row), then fill_span_list.
comment fill_quad Unused: fills the convex quadrilateral left_x, top_y / second_x, second_y / third_x, third_y / bottom_x, bottom_y (in order round it) with fill_color at 8 bpp: edges walked in 16.16 from the top vertex into polygon_span records at bitmap_draw_buffer, then filled; flat rows go to fill_span_8bpp or the triangle code. Keeps the vertices on the stack.
comment fill_span_at_point Unused: fills the one run through point_x, point_y up to border_color (nothing outside bitmap_window or on fill_color or border_color). At 8 bpp flood_fill_span does it; the 4 bpp nibble scans start from outcode (0) instead of point_x and read through right_cursor, which nothing sets: that path cannot work as written.
comment fill_span_at_point_fill_run Unused: fill_span_at_point's 4 bpp fill of x left_x to right_x from r14 with fill_color's low nibble: an odd first pixel (high nibble), an aligning byte, longs, a halfword, a byte, an even last pixel (low nibble). With one pixel left after the halfwords (or none after the aligning byte) it still writes the byte: 2 pixels too many.
comment fill_span_at_point_left_byte Unused: fill_span_at_point's 4 bpp left scan: the byte to the left (two pixels), its high nibble, the nearer odd pixel, first: fill_color or border_color there ends the run after it, as does the count's end; else its low nibble (fill_span_at_point_left_even_pixel).
comment fill_span_at_point_left_even_pixel Unused: fill_span_at_point's 4 bpp left scan: the low nibble, the farther even pixel: fill_color or border_color ends the run after it; else the next byte to the left (fill_span_at_point_left_byte) while the count lasts; then fill_span_at_point_scan_right.
comment fill_span_at_point_right_byte Unused: fill_span_at_point's 4 bpp right scan: the next byte to the right, its low nibble, the nearer even pixel, first: fill_color or border_color there ends the run before it, as does the count's end; else its high nibble (fill_span_at_point_right_odd_pixel).
comment fill_span_at_point_right_odd_pixel Unused: fill_span_at_point's 4 bpp right scan: the high nibble, the farther odd pixel: fill_color or border_color ends the run before it; else the next byte (fill_span_at_point_right_byte) while the count lasts; then fill_span_at_point_fill_run.
comment fill_span_at_point_scan_right Unused: fill_span_at_point's 4 bpp right scan from x right_x + 1 to bitmap_window_right, a byte (two nibbles) at a time through right_cursor (which nothing sets); with right_x already at the window's right edge straight to fill_span_at_point_fill_run.
comment fill_span_list Unused: fills span_count polygon_span records from bitmap_draw_buffer (bitmap address and length, a negative length skipping the row) with color at 8 bpp: an odd first byte, 16-byte blocks, then 8, 4, 2 and 1.
comment fill_span_list_from_r8 Unused: fill_span_list with polygon_color, the colour fill_quad keeps.
comment fill_triangle Unused: fills the triangle top_x, top_y / middle_x, middle_y / bottom_x, bottom_y with color at 8 bpp: sorts the points by y, sets current_player to bitmap_address (the base of the span addresses) and the polygon_span list at bitmap_draw_buffer, then fill_triangle_sorted.
comment fill_triangle_sorted Unused: the points sorted top to bottom: one row (fill_span_8bpp from the leftmost to the rightmost x) when all share y, fill_flat_top_triangle when the top two do; else both edges stepped in 16.16, a polygon_span (bitmap address, length) a row at span_cursor, turning at the middle point; then fill_span_list.
comment flood_fill Unused: scanline flood fill from seed_x, seed_y with fill_color up to border_color in bitmap_window (none when the seed is outside or either colour): the seed's span, then a ring queue of flood_fill_record spans in bitmap_draw_buffer (object_cursor in, last_object out) worked off a row above and below each; the queue reaches over string_queue.
comment flood_fill_push_span Unused: fills the run at r14 (x left_x) in the scanned row (flood_fill_span) and queues its flood_fill_record at object_cursor: direction and row y + direction, its right and left ends, the flood_fill_push_parent_* range; object_cursor wraps from 0xCCC4 to bitmap_draw_buffer. right_x and right_address come back at the run's right end.
comment flood_fill_scan_row Unused: scans row y + direction under or over the current span, from flood_fill_left_x to flood_fill_right_x (copied into the flood_fill_push_parent_* range): every run not in the fill or border colour goes through flood_fill_push_span, the scan going on 2 past its right end; hands back the x the scan reached.
comment flood_fill_scan_row_skip_parent Unused: a queued span's row in direction: toward its own flood_fill_direction the whole row (flood_fill_scan_row); back toward its parent only the parts left of flood_fill_parent_left_x and right of flood_fill_parent_right_x + 1, each run there through flood_fill_push_span.
comment flood_fill_skip_parent_right Unused: flood_fill_scan_row_skip_parent's right part: from flood_fill_parent_right_x + 1 to flood_fill_right_x, two pixels at a time, each run of fillable pixels pushed through flood_fill_push_span; hands back scan_x.
comment flood_fill_scan_seed_rows Unused: the seed span's neighbour rows: flood_fill_scan_row above (direction -1) when y is below window_top, and below (1) when y is above window_bottom; hands back the x the last scan reached.
comment flood_fill_scan_span_rows Unused: the same as flood_fill_scan_seed_rows for a span taken from the queue, through flood_fill_scan_row_skip_parent.
comment flood_fill_span Unused: the run through the pixel at r14 (x left_x) at 8 bpp: scans left to window_left and right to window_right up to the fill colour (fill_pattern) or border_color, then fills it (flood_fill_span_fill_run); left_x and r14 come back at its left end, right_x and right_address at its right end. Also fill_span_at_point's 8 bpp path.
comment flood_fill_span_fill_run Unused: fills the run from left_x to right_x with fill_pattern from r14: an odd first byte, 16-byte blocks, then 8, 4, 2 and 1; hands back the address of the last byte written.
comment flood_fill_span_left_pair Unused: flood_fill_span's left scan: the next two pixels to the left (a halfword before r14), the nearer one first: the fill or border colour there ends the run after it (flood_fill_span_set_left_x); else flood_fill_span_left_pixel for the farther one.
comment flood_fill_span_left_pixel Unused: flood_fill_span's left scan: the farther pixel of the pair (or an odd first one): the fill colour ends the run after it, the border colour or the count's end too (an odd last pixel checked first when pixel_count is odd); else the next pair (flood_fill_span_left_pair).
comment flood_fill_span_right_pair Unused: flood_fill_span's right scan: the next two pixels (a halfword at right_cursor), the nearer one first: the fill or border colour there ends the run before it (flood_fill_span_set_right_x); else flood_fill_span_right_pixel for the farther one.
comment flood_fill_span_right_pixel Unused: flood_fill_span's right scan: the farther pixel of the pair (or an odd first one): the fill colour ends the run before it, the border colour or the count's end too (an odd last pixel checked first when pixel_count is odd); else the next pair (flood_fill_span_right_pair).
comment flood_fill_span_scan_right Unused: flood_fill_span's right scan from the pixel after the seed (seed_address + 1) toward window_right, a pair at a time (flood_fill_span_right_pair, _right_pixel); with right_x already at window_right straight to flood_fill_span_fill_run.
comment flood_fill_span_set_left_x Unused: left_x -= seed_address - r14, the run's left end x (r14 on its first pixel), then flood_fill_span_scan_right.
comment flood_fill_span_set_right_x Unused: right_x += right_cursor - seed_address, the run's right end x (right_cursor on its last pixel), then flood_fill_span_fill_run; right_cursor comes back as the last byte written.
comment get_point_outcode Where point_x, point_y is outside bitmap_window, in outcode: 1 left, 2 right, 4 above, 8 below (0 inside); both come back sign-extended.
comment get_window_outcode Swaps the line's two points (start_x/_y with end_x/_y) and hands back in outcode where the new start is outside bitmap_window (get_point_outcode: 1 left, 2 right, 4 above, 8 below).
comment plot_circle_point_4bpp Unused: one of draw_circle's points at 4 bpp: the top two bits of current_player's mask, shifted out: the first plots, the second plots only inside the window (r14, window_top, _right, _bottom); the byte at (point_y << 8) + (point_x >> 1) + bitmap_base gets high_color in its high nibble at odd x, low_color in its low one at even x.
comment plot_circle_point_8bpp Unused: one of draw_circle's points at 8 bpp: the same test of current_player's top two bits, then color at (point_y << 9) + point_x + bitmap_base.
comment save_bitmap_rect Unused: meant to save the rectangle left, top to right, bottom of the bitmap (corners sorted) into buffer: a saved_bitmap_rect header (width in bits, * 8 at 8 bpp, * 4 kept to a byte at 4 bpp, and rows), then each row. The row copy is an instruction the V60 cannot run, so the C stops at invalid_operand on the first row.

# ======== stack slots ========
local boot 000043 s100004 initial_psw                    # 0, written to the stack and loaded into the PSW
local spawn_grate_step_debris 08BC09 s4 saved_record     # the piece's record, 8 bytes on, kept across next_random
